During their chat on the 'Sibling Revelry' podcast, both Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin delivered the bittersweet news: a sequel is nearly impossible. With Goodwin sharing that as she nears the big 5-0, the character's age dilemma hits closer to home than ever before. The duo Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin are best known for their 90s chick-flick film ‘Something Borrowed.’ In a season where old classics are getting remakes and prequels (‘Freakier Friday’ and ‘Practical Magic 2), fans had been wondering whether the two beloved stars would be open to reuniting for a sequel to ‘Something Borrowed’ or not. Recently in an interview, the two formally put all questions and rumors to rest. Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin share insights about ‘Something Borrowed’ sequel On November 24, Kate Hudson invited Goodwin on her and her brother, Oliver Hudson’s, podcast titled ‘Sibling Revelry’ in order to get candid and talk about her career as an actress. During one of the segments of the show, the conversation drifted to their 2011 release, ‘Something Borrowed.’ Hudson shared that she had mentioned the project on multiple occasions, but it never ended up happening. She added, “I was saying to Ollie that I get asked about [a sequel] on the [red] carpet all the time. I was on the carpet not that long ago, and they were like, ‘What’s the movie that you would want to do the sequel [to]? And I was like, ‘Well, Something Borrowed, we never got to do the sequel.” Ginnifer also added that she would no longer be open to a project like that anymore. She added, “I would not want to go back and do Something Blue at this point.” Kate ended up adding, “I mean, we’re kind of too old.” The two set the record straight during the podcast and shared how the project never happened, and they would no longer be interested in it as well. Goodwin even talked about how she had a monologue in the film about spiralling and turning 30, and that she would not feel okay with it as she is now turning 50. She further shared that, “My sons, their girlfriends at school, they’ve been learning the dance. I’ve got a bunch of 12 year olds… I show up, I’m the assistant librarian when I’m not doing other things. And I have shown up on campus and had the girls be like, Mrs. Dallas, look. ” About ‘Something Borrowed’ The film was originally based on a 2005 romantic comedy novel written by author Emily Griffin. A sequel book titled ‘Something Blue’ was also published, and a script was already in the works as per PopSugar; however, no updates have been shared about the sequel with the public, leading everyone to believe that the case is cold. most looking forward to in   you guessed it   2025       Just don t expect any Marvel or DC movies on here  I ll try to keep it short and sweet  but I do have a few honorable mentions that have me intrigued         DreamWorks Animation s DOG MAN  which is the spin off of CAPTAIN UNDERPANTS with an even weirder premise yet an interesting voice cast and style       January 31        A comedy currently referred to as UNTITLED TREY PARKER AND MATT STONE FILM  I am a big SOUTH PARK fan and I find it interesting that the creators are making a new movie with Kendrick Lamar of all people  but there s no title or premise announced yet       July 4        THE BATTLE OF BAKTAN CROSS from Paul Thomas Anderson  who I m not a big fan of  but his new movie is a crime drama thriller with an Oscar worthy cast and it s his first film in IMAX  Still  what is it about       August 8        Streaming movies that don t have a release date yet no matter how exciting they are like Guy Ritchie s star studded fantasy FOUNTAIN OF YOUTH on Apple TV  and Guillermo del Toro s FRANKENSTEIN on Netflix  I mean  we currently don t know if they re premiering this year or the next       Note that release dates are always subject to change and there could be surprise movies announced later in the year  Like remember last year when MOANA 2 was announced nine months before release  That was crazy and we might have something like this again  You never know       As of now  these are my 25 most anticipated movies of 2025                                                              25  HAPPY GILMORE 2      2025      The original 1996 comedy classic is arguably Adam Sandler s best film  but I never expected this of all movies to have a sequel and it just seems very unnecessary  The Sandman himself returns with Virginia the love interest  Otto the caddy  Hal L  the sadistic caretaker  and of course  Shooter McGavin  What is exciting about this project is the surprise teaser trailer we got on Christmas morning and the huge amount of cameos joining the main cast  So  why do I have it this low  The fact that I already mentioned how unneeded this sequel is especially after so long  the fact that this sequel is streaming on Netflix instead of coming to theatres from Universal like the original  the fear that this could have too many cameos like ZOOLANDER 2 which hurt that unnecessary sequel  and there s currently no release date  Well  at least we got a cool teaser and a confirmation that it s coming this year  I m guessing the summer in time for golf season  but we ll see  I just hope it s at least good                                                              24  LOVE HURTS      February 7      An action comedy starring Oscar winners Ke Huy Quan and Ariana DeBose might be enough to get butts in seats  I would still wait for the reviews  but the trailer has me intrigued  Quan is a successful realtor whose past as a violent hitman comes back to haunt him when DeBose as his former partner warns him that his gangster brother played by Daniel Wu is hunting him down  This looks like another action packed good time from 87North                                                              23  WOLF MAN      January 17      My first big movie of the year ought to be downright terrifying  After the collaboration between Leigh Whannell and Blumhouse on THE INVISIBLE MAN resulted in Universal s most successful reboot of their classic monsters a few weeks before the pandemic lockdowns began  they hope to recreate the same spooky magic with a modern take of THE WOLF MAN  What was supposed to be a Ryan Gosling project after a successful pitch  the movie stars Christopher Abbott as a father whose arm is clawed by a werewolf and begins to transform into something horrifying  Julia Garner plays his wife and the mother of their scared daughter  Even though Whannell mentioned using body horror movies like David Cronenberg s THE FLY as inspiration  which are always a big no for me  I m hoping it s not too graphic  I will hopefully see this in IMAX and it s good to know that Gosling is still producing                                                              22  THE BAD GUYS 2      August 1      DreamWorks Animation s newest franchise brings back The Bad Guys as they struggle to find trust and acceptance as The Good Guys  only to be forced to do  one last job  by an all female squad of criminals called The Bad Girls  The first movie based on the book series by Aaron Blabey was a good time and it looks like the sequel will take the zany action and comedy even further                                                              21  MERCY      August 15      Amazon MGM Studios  sci thriller filmed for IMAX sees Chris Pratt as a detective having to prove his innocence after being accused of a crime  There s no trailer yet  but it kinda sounds like a futuristic version of Harrison Ford s THE FUGITIVE  It s directed by Timur Bekmambetov and co stars Rebecca Ferguson and Annabelle Wallis                                                              20  THE RUNNING MAN      November 7      Set to be a proper adaptation of Stephen King s dystopian novel  this will be nothing like the Arnold Schwarzenegger movie of the 80s  Like the book  the new movie from Edgar Wright will focus on Ben Richards  a father who becomes a contestant on a deadly game show to win a billion dollars to save his terminally ill daughter  Contestants are chased around the world by murderous people known as Hunters and whoever survives for 30 days will take home the grand prize  Glen Powell will play Ben Richards and it features quite the supporting cast with Katy O Brian  Josh Brolin  Lee Pace  Michael Cera  Emilia Jones  and William H  Macy  Now I don t know if this movie will take place in 2025 like the book because the year we re about to go into is literally 2025  And yes  I know the book ends tragically  but maybe if we re lucky  this new adaptation could have a better ending  I mean if THE SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION can be a movie better than the book  why not this  Let s hope for the best                                                              19  FIVE NIGHTS AT FREDDY S 2      December 5      FNAF has become quite a cultural phenomenon that garnered a huge fanbase  Despite negative reviews from critics  fans and those curious like of the second game will see Josh Hutcherson and Matthew Lillard return as their characters  Freddy Fazbear  Bonnie  Chica  Foxy  and Mr  Cupcake are all coming back for round two with Toy Freddy stakes at hand  so let s go                                                              18  A MINECRAFT MOVIE      April 4      This is a controversial take  but even as someone who doesn t play the stars Jason Momoa  Emma Myers  Danielle Brooks  Jennifer Coolidge  Matt Berry  Kate McKinnon  and Jemaine Clement  The first trailer was incredibly hated for it s CGI  character designs  and live featurettes seemed to have earned a more positive response from viewers  I just hope this movie surprises everyone because I want to see this in IMAX with an edgy R rating  Robert Pattinson plays a guy named Mickey Barnes who is so desperate to leave Earth that he regretfully signs up to be an  expendable   a disposable employee where after one iteration dies  a new body is regenerated with most of their memories intact  When one of his  multiples  known as Mickey 17 unintentionally survives a human expedition to colonize an ice world  he Ginnifer Goodwin and Jason Bateman ’s return as Officer Judy Hopps and Nick Wilde in ‘Zootopia 2’ has been much appreciated by the public. The first film was released all the way back in 2016 and managed to garner a lot of love and attention worldwide. In a recent interview, the star delved into recording for the hit animated film and why she wishes for the next film to come sooner. Ginnifer Goodwin shares how she and Jason Bateman had to be separated while recording Ginnifer Goodwin, who voices the main character Judy Hopps, recently revealed how it was to record for the second installment of the franchise. While talking about her co-star Bateman with The Hollywood Reporter, the actress hilariously confessed that the two were not allowed to record their lines together and had to be separated every time. She further provided context, adding that, “I get the giggles really, really, really badly. I waste everyone’s time. He can’t not make me laugh. They built these booths where they are going to be able to put us. If we can get a third one, they can put us in the same space, and I won’t ruin all the takes because if I’m laughing, they can isolate that sound out. We have to do this just so I can experience it and not just have to wonder what it is he did in his recording. ” Ginnifer Goodwin opens up about the film and expectations for the third installment The second installment of the film was released almost a decade after the first film, and Goodwin revealed during the interview that she had been itching to get back in the studio. “I would call them every year and I’d be like, ‘Is this the year?’ And they’d be like, ‘We’re really busy with a lot of things, just hold on tight.’ So I was waiting and waiting,” she further revealed. While talking about the next film, she shared that the wait time is not as long and that she is “trying to manifest a number three, after a much shorter break. Goodwin, who voices Judy Hopps in both 2016’s Zootopia and its upcoming sequel, wowed in an off-the-shoulder cream gown with floral embellishments along the bodice. The team working behind the first Zootopia film ignored the directions they were given to add certain number of puns in the write up. In conversation with SFX magazine, he added that the first movie featured only five puns, but they have taken it to a whole new level for the second film. "I do love a pun. In the new sequel featuring Jason Batman and Ginnifer Goodwin, besides the puns in character names and dialogues, audience will get to see signs reimagined versions of iconic brands. While talking about Zootopia 2 , Bush said, "You\'ll see a ton of advertisements and brand labels. It is aggressive and we love it." Without giving much spoilers, the screenwriter added that the most iconic pun appears when Nick is look on something called HuluZoo streaming service. Directed by Bush and Byron Howard, the upcoming animated includes voiceovers by Shakira Macaulay Culkin, Robert Irwin, Ke Huy Quan and many more. Zootopia 2 is slated to release on November 26. For those dreamers wishing for a sequel to 'Something Borrowed', it's time to temper those expectations. During their chat on the 'Sibling Revelry' podcast, both Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin delivered the bittersweet news: a sequel is nearly impossible. With Goodwin sharing that as she nears the big 5-0, the character's age dilemma hits closer to home than ever before. The duo Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin are best known for their 90s chick-flick film ‘Something Borrowed.’ In a season where old classics are getting remakes and prequels (‘Freakier Friday’ and ‘Practical Magic 2), fans had been wondering whether the two beloved stars would be open to reuniting for a sequel to ‘Something Borrowed’ or not. Recently in an interview, the two formally put all questions and rumors to rest. Kate Hudson and Ginnifer Goodwin share insights about ‘Something Borrowed’ sequel On November 24, Kate Hudson invited Goodwin on her and her brother, Oliver Hudson’s, podcast titled ‘Sibling Revelry’ in order to get candid and talk about her career as an actress. During one of the segments of the show, the conversation drifted to their 2011 release, ‘Something Borrowed.’ Hudson shared that she had mentioned the project on multiple occasions, but it never ended up happening. She added, “I was saying to Ollie that I get asked about [a sequel] on the [red] carpet all the time. I was on the carpet not that long ago, and they were like, ‘What’s the movie that you would want to do the sequel [to]? And I was like, ‘Well, Something Borrowed, we never got to do the sequel.” Ginnifer also added that she would no longer be open to a project like that anymore. She added, “I would not want to go back and do Something Blue at this point.” Kate ended up adding, “I mean, we’re kind of too old.” The two set the record straight during the podcast and shared how the project never happened, and they would no longer be interested in it as well. Goodwin even talked about how she had a monologue in the film about spiralling and turning 30, and that she would not feel okay with it as she is now turning 50. She further shared that, “My sons, their girlfriends at school, they’ve been learning the dance. I’ve got a bunch of 12 year olds… I show up, I’m the assistant librarian when I’m not doing other things. And I have shown up on campus and had the girls be like, Mrs. Dallas, look. ” About ‘Something Borrowed’ The film was originally based on a 2005 romantic comedy novel written by author Emily Griffin. A sequel book titled ‘Something Blue’ was also published, and a script was already in the works as per PopSugar; however, no updates have been shared about the sequel with the public, leading everyone to believe that the case is cold. Fergus Dennehy Kerryman Mon 17 Nov 2025 at 18:00 Presentation Secondary School Listowel proudly announced that student Grace Foley has qualified for the SciFest National Final, which will take place at the Marino Institute of Education, Dublin, on Friday, November 21. Grace’s innovative and thought-provoking project, titled Yummy, Yummy Uh Oh – Microplastics in My Tummy , explores the presence and potential impact of microplastics in the human food chain. Her work, which highlights a growing environmental and health concern, first gained recognition in the Biological and Ecological category at the BT Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition (BTYSE) last January. In April, Grace’s outstanding research and scientific curiosity were further recognised when she was awarded the coveted Best Project runner up Award at SciFest in TUS Limerick. This success has now earned her a place among the top young scientists in Ireland as she competes at the SciFest National Final. Grace is currently applying the final touches to her research and is set to represent both Presentation Secondary School, Listowel, and Kerry on the national stage. Her dedication, creativity, and commitment to scientific exploration continue to inspire her peers and teachers alike. The school community extends its full support to Grace as she prepares to showcase her project at the national final in Dublin, wishing her every success as she continues her journey in science. School in Listowel. Fergus Dennehy Kerryman Mon 17 Nov 2025 at 18:00 Presentation Secondary School Listowel proudly announced that student Grace Foley has qualified for the SciFest National Final, which will take place at the Marino Institute of Education, Dublin, on Friday, November 21. Grace’s innovative and thought-provoking project, titled Yummy, Yummy Uh Oh – Microplastics in My Tummy , explores the presence and potential impact of microplastics in the human food chain. Her work, which highlights a growing environmental and health concern, first gained recognition in the Biological and Ecological category at the BT Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition (BTYSE) last January. In April, Grace’s outstanding research and scientific curiosity were further recognised when she was awarded the coveted Best Project runner up Award at SciFest in TUS Limerick. This success has now earned her a place among the top young scientists in Ireland as she competes at the SciFest National Final. Grace is currently applying the final touches to her research and is set to represent both Presentation Secondary School, Listowel, and Kerry on the national stage. Her dedication, creativity, and commitment to scientific exploration continue to inspire her peers and teachers alike. The school community extends its full support to Grace as she prepares to showcase her project at the national final in Dublin, wishing her every success as she continues her journey in science. news_text_raw: ["‘Rick and Morty’s Spencer Grammer Wants to Join ‘The Simpsons’ as Sideshow Bob’s Nepo Baby | Cracked.com Menu Search Search Search Trivia & Jokes Movies & TV Science & History Videos Newsletter My Account Search Trivia & Jokes Movies & TV Science & History Videos Newsletter Producers Threw Down Over ‘A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving' Moment 15 Common Myths and Misconceptions About Thanksgiving This Is The Best Episode Of ‘Veep’ I Made Those Puppets for Eddie Murphy 15 Differences Between the 'Alice's Restaurant’ Movie and the Real-Life Story ‘Rick and Morty’s Spencer Grammer Wants to Join ‘The Simpsons’ as Sideshow Bob’s Nepo Baby Ok, that’s not a bad idea November 23, 2025 Add Cracked to Google JM McNab If years of absorbing full-body rake blows haven't rendered Sideshow Bob infertile, Spencer Grammer has a story idea for The Simpsons . Grammer, of course, is the voice actress behind Rick and Morty ’s Summer Smith. She also happens to be the daughter of Kelsey Grammer, who, when he’s not busy making awkward Frasier -themed commercials , voices Bart Simpson’s archenemy, Robert Underdunk Terwilliger. Spencer Grammer recently guested on Nancy Cartwright’s Simpsons Declassified podcast, where she proposed a way that she might join the cast of the long-running Fox show. Don't Miss These Are The Most Glaring Omissions on ‘Variety’s 100 Best Comedies List Authors JM McNab Published 11/26/2025 Kevin Hart Probably Wants His Appearance On Ziwe Back Authors Opheli Garcia Lawler Published 11/25/2025 'South Park' Sells Out To The Saudi Royal Family Authors Keegan Kelly Published 11/26/2025 “I secretly wish that Sideshow Bob had a daughter, and that I got to play his daughter,” Grammer told Cartwright. “And she enacts revenge for all of the years that he left to pursue killing Bart, because she’s so angry that she was abandoned, and he was just obsessed with this guy Bart.” In Grammer's pitch, Sideshow Bob’s daughter, enraged over her father’s fixation on another kid, ends up trying to kill Bart herself. “That’s my dream,” Grammer added, pointing out that it’s a “super nepo baby” idea. “Like fully immersed in the nepo baby,” she added. “Spencer, I think we should meet again after this podcast,” a visibly impressed Cartwright responded. When pressed for more details, Grammer explained that Sideshow Bob’s daughter should be “slightly older than Bart, basically the same age as Summer, like 17. So he could maybe have a crush on her, you know?” She also suggested that the character could be named “Sabrina” as a nod to Cartwright’s niece, Sabrina Carpenter. Cartwright put forward “Bobbi” as another possibility. Advertisement The Simpsons has explored stories about the fruit of Sideshow Bob’s loins in the past. Back in season 17’s “The Italian Bob,” we learned that Krutsty’s former sidekick started a family, including a son, little Gino Terwilliger. Advertisement Advertisement But after the character appeared in just two episodes, the Simpsons writers seem to have largely forgotten about little Gino. Plus, hiring Grammer to play Sideshow Bob’s daughter would make a lot of sense, not just because she’s a talented voice actress herself, but because The Simpsons has a long history of stunt casting Bob’s family members. Advertisement Finally, given that Spencer Grammer was estranged from her father between the ages of 4 and 16 , her pitch about Sideshow Bob’s murderous impulses leading to childhood abandonment might be somewhat personal. Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for SCAD/TNS file Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Kelsey Grammer is a dad again at 70: He welcomes 8th child, 4th with Kayte Walsh By Alexandra Del Rosario Los Angeles Times (TNS) Oct 28, 2025 Oct 28, 2025 Updated Oct 28, 2025 Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Kayte Walsh, left, and Kelsey Grammer in February 2024. Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for SCAD/TNS file Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Septuagenarian TV star Kelsey Grammer is still growing his family, most recently with the arrival of his newest child. The beloved portrayer of Frasier Crane on “Cheers” and “Frasier,” who turned 70 in February, is now a father of eight. Grammer announced he and wife Kayte Walsh welcomed their fourth child together during his appearance on the “Pod Meets World” podcast.” We just had our fourth one, it just became eight kids,” he said during the podcast episode, published Monday. “Christopher, that’s (who) just joined the family.” The Emmy-winning TV veteran said his newest son arrived “three days” before the episode taped and joked with podcast hosts Rider Strong, Danielle Fishel and Will Friedle that he has “clusters” of children of different ages. Grammer and Walsh, 46, married in 2011 and also share a teenage daughter and two sons. People reported in June that the couple was expecting a child again, publishing photos of the two taking a stroll through London. The five-time Emmy winner has been married four times. Before Walsh, he was married to dancer-model Camille Donatacci. He was also briefly married to Leigh-Anne Csuhany, and dance instructor Doreen Alderman before that. His seven other children, the eldest being actor Spencer Grammer, hail from those previous relationships. The sitcom star became a grandfather in October 2011, when his son Spencer welcomed a son with ex-husband James Hesketh. In the past, Grammer has been open about the “beauty of being an older dad.” He told the Guardian in 2018 that raising children later in life he feels fortunate to “get a chance to kinda try it again . That’s been a real gift .” The actor announced the arrival of his eighth child while promoting his book “Karen: A Brother Remembers,” released in May, about the brutal murder of his sister at age 18 and his lifelong battle with grief. During the episode, Fishel asked the actor how much his children knew about his late sister. He explained his older children have varying degrees of knowledge about his sister, while his younger kids will have to wait to learn more and read his book. “Some of the stuff is too brutal, they don’t really need to be exposed to that yet,” he said. Throughout the podcast episode, Grammer also recalled the proceedings in his sister’s case and learning how to process the loss while delivering laughs on TV. “I didn’t walk around talking about it a lot, it’s been with me since the day it happened,” he said. Kelsey added that it’s been “awesome and fantastic” having a fourth child with his wife of 14 years , with whom he also shares kids Faith , 12, Gabriel , 10, and James , 8. The Cheers actor first shared the news that Kayte, 46, had given birth in October. "It was like three days ago," Kelsey —who’s also dad to daughter Spencer , 41, with Doreen Alderman ; Greer , 33, with Barrie Buckner ; as well as Mason , 23, and Jude , 20, with Camille Grammer —shared during an appearance on the Pod Meets World podcast . "Christopher\'s just joined the family." He added , “It just became eight kids." read Kelsey Grammer and More Famous Dads Who Welcomed Babies Later in Life And becoming a dad again later in life gave him the chance to reflect on his relationship with his older children. "I have neglected a couple of the kids in my life, especially the first two," Kelsey confessed to People in May. "I\'m trying to make up for a little of it now. I\'m still their dad, so you can always have [a] chance to show up." Chelsea Lauren/Shutterstock Plus, he’s learned how he needs to parent differently when it comes to the younger members of his clan. "I probably should have been a little more clear and maybe less tolerant with the older ones," he explained. "I\'m pretty tolerant with the young ones, but I\'m clear about how there\'s certain expectations and certain ways to navigate through a social situation.” The Emmy winner noted that he’s encouraging his younger children to “keep it close to the vest and play it straight.” “I’m a little more specific with them about doing their studies and being prepared,” he added. “[I tell them], \'What\'s your job in life? Showing up.\'" For more on Kelsey’s expansive family, keep reading. Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images Spencer Grammer Kelsey Grammer married dance instructor Doreen Alderman in 1982 and they welcomed daughter Spencer Grammer on Oct. 9, 1983. Though they didn\'t divorce until 1990, Kelsey and Doreen separated not long after Spencer was born—and the actor has since admitted to not being as present as he could have been the first time around. "I have neglected a couple of the kids in my life, especially the first two," Kelsey told People in May 2025. "I\'m trying to make up for a little of it now. I\'m still their dad, so you can always have [a] chance to show up." Spencer Grammer/Instagram Spencer was married to firefighter James Hesketh from 2011 to 2017 and they share son Emmett , born in October 2011. An actress and singer known for Greek and providing the voice of Summer on Rick and Morty , Spencer fulfilled her dream of acting alongside Kelsey when they played father and daughter in 2022\'s The 12 Days of Christmas Eve . "I haven\'t done any other Christmas movies, so it was my first experience in the Christmas world, but it made it momentous for me to actually do a movie with my father," Spencer told E! News at the time. "I\'ve always wanted to work with him." In July 2024, she mourned the death of her former stepdad Dr. Bill Skinner , in her life since she was 5 even after he and her mother split up. "He has been there for me my whole life…no matter what I needed," Spencer wrote on Instagram . "He was there. I always got to be his kid. He always gave me a hug, always listened, always believed in me, and always supported me." Barry King/Getty Images Greer Grammer Kandace Greer Grammer was born Feb. 15, 1992, to Kelsey and makeup artist Barrie Buckner . That relationship was short-lived, as the Cheers actor married Leigh-Anne Csuhany that September—a union that was annulled at the groom\'s behest in 1993. "For the most part, I had a regular childhood," Greer told Glamour in 2015 . "Sometimes though I would wonder if people wanted to be my friend because they liked me or because of who my dad was." While her father expressed his regret for past neglect, Greer—who appeared on a 2024 episode of the Paramount+ Frasier reboot—followed closely in his footsteps. “I remember going to tapings of Frasier when I was around 4,” the Awkard actress told Nylon in 2014. “I knew I was at my dad’s work, but I didn’t get that he was acting for TV. It wasn’t until the second grade that it really hit me.” Monica Schipper/GA/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images Asked about the best advice her famous father had given her over the years about their shared profession, Greer told Stage Buddy in 2021, "He gives me a lot of advice but the best was one time he told me to make sure that I act because I love it. He said \'act for the right reasons.\' One time we had a lengthy conversation where he was honest with me and talked to me about how unfair and cruel Hollywood can be to women, he said, “Don’t let it get to you.\' I still get emotional when I think about it." Amanda Edwards/Getty Images Mason Grammer Kelsey married Camille Donatacci in 1997 and they welcomed daughter Mason Grammer on Oct. 24, 2001, via surrogate. The end of their marriage in 2010 became engrossing fodder for The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills , which counted Camille as an original cast member when it premiered that year. Mason, a model and graduate of Emerson College, said in 2018 that her relationship with Kelsey suffered in the wake of her parents\' messy split, but they had since repaired their bond. “It was the hardest time of my life,” she recalled to Genlux , per Page Six . “I changed a lot after that. I had to grow up faster because I had a lot more responsibilities. My dad wasn’t around, so I didn’t see him much, and my mom had such a hard time. I became my younger brother’s mom. Everyone was on edge. My parents still don’t talk." Camille, who\'s been married to second husband David Meyer since 2018, did throw a compliment her ex\'s way, telling Page Six that Mason was "a really good student" and she "must have gotten that from [her] dad because I don’t have that kind of discipline at times!” Rich Polk/Getty Images for IMDb Jude Grammer Kelsey and Camille welcomed son Jude Grammer on Aug. 28, 2004, also via surrogate. The youngest of Kelsey\'s non-minor children is more private than his older sisters, but Camille told Page Six in 2018 that Jude "wants to be like his dad, an actor." But, she added, "He doesn’t like being in pictures right now. He hides. If I get a picture of him out of him, I’m lucky!" Jason Merritt/Getty Images For W Magazine Faith Grammer Two weeks after his divorce from Camille was finalized, Kelsey married flight attendant Kayte Walsh on Feb. 25, 2011. Their daughter Faith Evangeline Elisa Grammer was born July 13, 2012, the couple explaining that, while they had originally announced they were expecting twins, "tragically we lost the little boy shortly thereafter." Five years later, Kelsey opened Faith American Brewery in upstate New York. "My daughter\'s name is Faith, but there\'s also action in Faith. Faith is something you have to fight for," he explained to Fox Business . "We fought for this beautiful child in our lives, and she\'s our first child. And the idea of America is still something I\'m willing to fight for." Donna Ward/Getty Images Gabriel Grammer Kelsey Gabriel Elias Grammer was born July 22, 2014, and the boy\'s father let it be known that he and Kayte were just getting started with two kids. “I can’t imagine not trying for more because it’s been incredible," Kelsey, who\'s 25 years older than his third bride, told People when Gabriel was 5 weeks old. “As soon as [he] came out, Kayte and I were going, ‘Yeah, let’s do another one.\'” (The actor born Allen Kelsey Grammer also said they\'d be following his family\'s tradition of calling their boys by their middle name.) "It’s just this overwhelming gratification of being close to life like this. It just gives you such hope and joy,” Kelsey gushed. “I’ve never felt more alive or more serenely happy than in the throes of life with these young people. I really enjoy it.” Broadimage/Shutterstock James Grammer Kayte and Kelsey\'s family grew again on Nov. 14, 2016, with the birth of son Auden James Grammer . And the Frasier star\'s older kids were all for it. "My dad\'s always wanted a huge family," Greer told Entertainment Tonight two months before James arrived. "Him and Kayte are such great parents together, and they have all these little ones, and they love them so much. They\'re the cutest kids, Faith and Gabe. I\'m excited for them to have another one, another crazy baby." Mason said Kelsey "becomes a better dad after every child,” telling Closer in 2018, “When I grew up, he was very strict. Now he’s more relaxed with my younger siblings. It’s a blast!" JAMIE LAMOR THOMPSON/Shutterstock Christopher Grammer Kelsey revealed on the Pod Meets World podcast in October 2025 that he and Kayte " just had our fourth one , so it just became eight kids." Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for SCAD/TNS file Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Facebook Twitter Linkedin SMS Email Print Save Septuagenarian TV star Kelsey Grammer is still growing his family, most recently with the arrival of his newest child. The beloved portrayer of Frasier Crane on “Cheers” and “Frasier,” who turned 70 in February, is now a father of eight. Grammer announced he and wife Kayte Walsh welcomed their fourth child together during his appearance on the “Pod Meets World” podcast.” We just had our fourth one, it just became eight kids,” he said during the podcast episode, published Monday. “Christopher, that’s (who) just joined the family.” The Emmy-winning TV veteran said his newest son arrived “three days” before the episode taped and joked with podcast hosts Rider Strong, Danielle Fishel and Will Friedle that he has “clusters” of children of different ages. Grammer and Walsh, 46, married in 2011 and also share a teenage daughter and two sons. People reported in June that the couple was expecting a child again, publishing photos of the two taking a stroll through London. The five-time Emmy winner has been married four times. Before Walsh, he was married to dancer-model Camille Donatacci. He was also briefly married to Leigh-Anne Csuhany, and dance instructor Doreen Alderman before that. His seven other children, the eldest being actor Spencer Grammer, hail from those previous relationships. The sitcom star became a grandfather in October 2011, when his son Spencer welcomed a son with ex-husband James Hesketh. In the past, Grammer has been open about the “beauty of being an older dad.” He told the Guardian in 2018 that raising children later in life he feels fortunate to “get a chance to kinda try it again . That’s been a real gift .” The actor announced the arrival of his eighth child while promoting his book “Karen: A Brother Remembers,” released in May, about the brutal murder of his sister at age 18 and his lifelong battle with grief. During the episode, Fishel asked the actor how much his children knew about his late sister. He explained his older children have varying degrees of knowledge about his sister, while his younger kids will have to wait to learn more and read his book. “Some of the stuff is too brutal, they don’t really need to be exposed to that yet,” he said. Throughout the podcast episode, Grammer also recalled the proceedings in his sister’s case and learning how to process the loss while delivering laughs on TV. “I didn’t walk around talking about it a lot, it’s been with me since the day it happened,” he said. "The family\'s ecstatic," the 70-year-old told People in an interview published Nov. 5. "We\'re all really having a great time. It\'s really lovely." Kelsey added that it’s been “awesome and fantastic” having a fourth child with his wife of 14 years , with whom he also shares kids Faith , 12, Gabriel , 10, and James , 8. The Cheers actor first shared the news that Kayte, 46, had given birth in October. "It was like three days ago," Kelsey —who’s also dad to daughter Spencer , 41, with Doreen Alderman ; Greer , 33, with Barrie Buckner ; as well as Mason , 23, and Jude , 20, with Camille Grammer —shared during an appearance on the Pod Meets World podcast . "Christopher\'s just joined the family." He added , “It just became eight kids." read Kelsey Grammer and More Famous Dads Who Welcomed Babies Later in Life And becoming a dad again later in life gave him the chance to reflect on his relationship with his older children. "I have neglected a couple of the kids in my life, especially the first two," Kelsey confessed to People in May. "I\'m trying to make up for a little of it now. I\'m still their dad, so you can always have [a] chance to show up." Chelsea Lauren/Shutterstock Plus, he’s learned how he needs to parent differently when it comes to the younger members of his clan. "I probably should have been a little more clear and maybe less tolerant with the older ones," he explained. "I\'m pretty tolerant with the young ones, but I\'m clear about how there\'s certain expectations and certain ways to navigate through a social situation.” The Emmy winner noted that he’s encouraging his younger children to “keep it close to the vest and play it straight.” “I’m a little more specific with them about doing their studies and being prepared,” he added. “[I tell them], \'What\'s your job in life? Showing up.\'" For more on Kelsey’s expansive family, keep reading. Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images Spencer Grammer Kelsey Grammer married dance instructor Doreen Alderman in 1982 and they welcomed daughter Spencer Grammer on Oct. 9, 1983. Though they didn\'t divorce until 1990, Kelsey and Doreen separated not long after Spencer was born—and the actor has since admitted to not being as present as he could have been the first time around. "I have neglected a couple of the kids in my life, especially the first two," Kelsey told People in May 2025. "I\'m trying to make up for a little of it now. I\'m still their dad, so you can always have [a] chance to show up." Spencer Grammer/Instagram Spencer was married to firefighter James Hesketh from 2011 to 2017 and they share son Emmett , born in October 2011. An actress and singer known for Greek and providing the voice of Summer on Rick and Morty , Spencer fulfilled her dream of acting alongside Kelsey when they played father and daughter in 2022\'s The 12 Days of Christmas Eve . "I haven\'t done any other Christmas movies, so it was my first experience in the Christmas world, but it made it momentous for me to actually do a movie with my father," Spencer told E! News at the time. "I\'ve always wanted to work with him." In July 2024, she mourned the death of her former stepdad Dr. Bill Skinner , in her life since she was 5 even after he and her mother split up. "He has been there for me my whole life…no matter what I needed," Spencer wrote on Instagram . "He was there. I always got to be his kid. He always gave me a hug, always listened, always believed in me, and always supported me." Barry King/Getty Images Greer Grammer Kandace Greer Grammer was born Feb. 15, 1992, to Kelsey and makeup artist Barrie Buckner . That relationship was short-lived, as the Cheers actor married Leigh-Anne Csuhany that September—a union that was annulled at the groom\'s behest in 1993. "For the most part, I had a regular childhood," Greer told Glamour in 2015 . "Sometimes though I would wonder if people wanted to be my friend because they liked me or because of who my dad was." While her father expressed his regret for past neglect, Greer—who appeared on a 2024 episode of the Paramount+ Frasier reboot—followed closely in his footsteps. “I remember going to tapings of Frasier when I was around 4,” the Awkard actress told Nylon in 2014. “I knew I was at my dad’s work, but I didn’t get that he was acting for TV. It wasn’t until the second grade that it really hit me.” Monica Schipper/GA/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images Asked about the best advice her famous father had given her over the years about their shared profession, Greer told Stage Buddy in 2021, "He gives me a lot of advice but the best was one time he told me to make sure that I act because I love it. He said \'act for the right reasons.\' One time we had a lengthy conversation where he was honest with me and talked to me about how unfair and cruel Hollywood can be to women, he said, “Don’t let it get to you.\' I still get emotional when I think about it." Amanda Edwards/Getty Images Mason Grammer Kelsey married Camille Donatacci in 1997 and they welcomed daughter Mason Grammer on Oct. 24, 2001, via surrogate. The end of their marriage in 2010 became engrossing fodder for The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills , which counted Camille as an original cast member when it premiered that year. Mason, a model and graduate of Emerson College, said in 2018 that her relationship with Kelsey suffered in the wake of her parents\' messy split, but they had since repaired their bond. “It was the hardest time of my life,” she recalled to Genlux , per Page Six . “I changed a lot after that. I had to grow up faster because I had a lot more responsibilities. My dad wasn’t around, so I didn’t see him much, and my mom had such a hard time. I became my younger brother’s mom. Everyone was on edge. My parents still don’t talk." Camille, who\'s been married to second husband David Meyer since 2018, did throw a compliment her ex\'s way, telling Page Six that Mason was "a really good student" and she "must have gotten that from [her] dad because I don’t have that kind of discipline at times!” Rich Polk/Getty Images for IMDb Jude Grammer Kelsey and Camille welcomed son Jude Grammer on Aug. 28, 2004, also via surrogate. The youngest of Kelsey\'s non-minor children is more private than his older sisters, but Camille told Page Six in 2018 that Jude "wants to be like his dad, an actor." But, she added, "He doesn’t like being in pictures right now. He hides. If I get a picture of him out of him, I’m lucky!" Jason Merritt/Getty Images For W Magazine Faith Grammer Two weeks after his divorce from Camille was finalized, Kelsey married flight attendant Kayte Walsh on Feb. 25, 2011. Their daughter Faith Evangeline Elisa Grammer was born July 13, 2012, the couple explaining that, while they had originally announced they were expecting twins, "tragically we lost the little boy shortly thereafter." Five years later, Kelsey opened Faith American Brewery in upstate New York. "My daughter\'s name is Faith, but there\'s also action in Faith. Faith is something you have to fight for," he explained to Fox Business . "We fought for this beautiful child in our lives, and she\'s our first child. And the idea of America is still something I\'m willing to fight for." Donna Ward/Getty Images Gabriel Grammer Kelsey Gabriel Elias Grammer was born July 22, 2014, and the boy\'s father let it be known that he and Kayte were just getting started with two kids. “I can’t imagine not trying for more because it’s been incredible," Kelsey, who\'s 25 years older than his third bride, told People when Gabriel was 5 weeks old. “As soon as [he] came out, Kayte and I were going, ‘Yeah, let’s do another one.\'” (The actor born Allen Kelsey Grammer also said they\'d be following his family\'s tradition of calling their boys by their middle name.) "It’s just this overwhelming gratification of being close to life like this. It just gives you such hope and joy,” Kelsey gushed. “I’ve never felt more alive or more serenely happy than in the throes of life with these young people. I really enjoy it.” Broadimage/Shutterstock James Grammer Kayte and Kelsey\'s family grew again on Nov. 14, 2016, with the birth of son Auden James Grammer . And the Frasier star\'s older kids were all for it. "My dad\'s always wanted a huge family," Greer told Entertainment Tonight two months before James arrived. "Him and Kayte are such great parents together, and they have all these little ones, and they love them so much. They\'re the cutest kids, Faith and Gabe. I\'m excited for them to have another one, another crazy baby." Mason said Kelsey "becomes a better dad after every child,” telling Closer in 2018, “When I grew up, he was very strict. Now he’s more relaxed with my younger siblings. It’s a blast!" news_text_raw: ["Deadline Print Article deadline-logo-svg Print ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Season 2 Sets Premiere Date At Apple TV With First-Look Photos At Rita Wilson & Judy Greer By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About ‘Percy Jackson And The Olympians’ Season 2 So Far ‘Zootopia 2’ Review: Disney Sequel Herds Familiar Themes While Successfully Expanding Animated Animal World From Metallica To Kate Bush, ‘Stranger Things’ Biggest Musical Moments Weave Into Spotify Experience Ahead Of Season 5 Launch View All November 5, 2025 7:00am L-R: Angourie Rice and Jennifer Garner in 'The Last Thing He Told Me' Season 2 Apple TV The Last Thing He Told Me Season 2 will return to Apple TV next year, and Rita Wilson has joined the cast for the next installment. The second season of the drama series, based on Laura Dave’s forthcoming sequel novel The First Time I Saw Him , will premiere Friday, February 20, 2026. There will be eight episodes. Related Stories News Everything We Know About ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Season 2 Casting ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Casts Judy Greer For Season 2 Season 2 will pick up as Owen Michaels (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau) shows up after five years on the run, initiating a race for Hannah Hall (Jennifer Garner) and her stepdaughter Bailey (Angourie Rice) to reunite their family “before the past catches up to them,” as the logline teases. The First Time I Saw Him will publish January 6, 2026, providing a hint at what’s to come for Hannah, Owen, Bailey and more ahead of the Season 2 premiere. Season 1 — which debuted in April 2023 — ended with Owen silently and subtly signaling to Hannah that he was still around by walking through her exhibition heavily disguised. Hannah had made a deal with Bailey’s grandfather Nicholas Bell (played by David Morse) that no harm would come to any of the three of them if Owen agreed to stay far away from Bailey. This is where Dave’s first novel, The Last Thing He Told Me , ended as well. Newcomers in addition to Judy Greer, whose casting Deadline first announced , and Wilson include Michael Galante, John Noble, and Luke Kirby. Missing from the returners is Aisha Tyler, who played Hannah’s best friend Jules Nichols. Season 2 is executive produced by co-showrunners Josh Singer and Aaron Zelman alongside Hello Sunshine’s Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter. Star Garner also executive produces. Zelman joins Season 2 as co-showrunner. The Last Thing He Told Me is produced by 20th Television and Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine, a part of Candle Media. Created and adapted by Laura Dave, alongside Academy Award-winning co-creator Josh Singer, The Last Thing He Told Me was the first collaboration between the married Dave and Singer, who both serve as executive producers. Aaron Zelman, Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard also serve as executive producers. The Lionsgate dystopian drama, adapted by JT Mollner from Stephen King’s early novel, hinges on the emotional dynamics among a group of teenage competitors forced to walk until only one remains. The filmmakers believe the film’s power lies not in traditional leads but in the collective experience — a choice they think is best reflected by submitting the ensemble together. Submitting the entire cast together highlights the filmmakers’ confidence in casting director Rich Delia, whose work stitching together a cohesive ensemble of emerging talent is expected to be a focal point of the campaign. The young actors deliver varied responses to the story’s brutal marathon. A second season of the buzzy Jennifer Garner -led series has filmed and will debut in early 2026, almost three years after Season 1 made its debut. Season 2 is based on Laura Dave \'s forthcoming novel The First Time I Saw Him , a sequel to her 2021 book The Last Thing He Told Me , which served as the basis for the television project. The original season marked the first collaboration between Dave and Josh Singer , the married couple who serve as executive producers alongside Garner and Hello Sunshine\'s Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter . For Season 2, Aaron Zelman joins as co-showrunner and executive producer with Singer. Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard are additional executive producers. Jennifer Garner Apple TV What\'s the plot? The last time we checked in on Hannah Hall (Garner), she was working at her art gallery when a heavily bearded man appeared, whom she immediately recognized as her missing husband, Owen ( Nikolaj Coster-Waldau ). He briefly touched her hand and whispered, "The could-have-been boys still love you," a callback to an earlier conversation about her exes. When Season 2 picks up, Hannah and her stepdaughter Bailey ( Angourie Rice ) find themselves in a terrifying race to figure out how to reunite their family before the past catches up to them. Who\'s in the cast? Garner, Coster-Waldau, and Rice are all back from Season 1, reprising their roles as three members of a dysfunctional family, as Hannah and Bailey are still searching for the missing Owen. Also returning is David Morse as Nicholas Bell, Owen\'s former father-in-law and Bailey\'s grandfather who has ties to the mafia. It\'s not yet known whether Victor Garber , Garner\'s Alias costar who popped up in Season 1 as Prof. Tobias Cookman, will return for the sequel. New additions to the cast for Season 2 include Rita Wilson , Judy Greer , Augusto Aguilera , Josh Hamilton , Nick Hargrove , Michael Galante , John Noble , Michael Hyatt , and Luke Kirby . What is the premiere date? Mark your calendar for Feb. 20, 2026, as that\'s when Season 2 will debut on Apple TV. That is almost three years after Season 1 launched on April 14, 2023. How many episodes? While the first season consisted of seven episodes, the upcoming season is slightly longer at eight episodes. Think of how much additional drama the writers can pack into that extra hour! First-look photos On Nov. 5, Apple TV released the first set of photos for Season 2 of The Last Thing He Told Me . The high-res images showcase Garner, Coster-Waldau, Rice, Wilson, and Greer. Eagle-eyed fans will notice the Eiffel Tower in the background of one of the pics, suggesting Garner\'s character will travel to Paris at some point. A video trailer will be unveiled at a later date. Based on the novel by Laura Dave , who developed the show with Josh Singer, The Last Thing He Told Me centers on Hannah Hall (Jennifer Garner) and her young stepdaughter after the mysterious disappearance of her husband. Debuting in April 2023 and consisting of seven episodes, the adaptation made a splash upon its premiere. It became Apple\'s most-watched limited series since the streaming service\'s debut in 2019, speeding up talks for The Last Thing He Told Me season 2. Apple reveals that The Last Thing He Told Me season 2 will premiere on Friday, February 20, 2026, and will consist of eight episodes. The photos, included below, reveal Garner\'s reunion with her 13 Going on 30 co-star Judy Greer. Based on the upcoming novel The First Time I Saw Him by Laura Dave, the upcoming episodes pick up as Hannah\'s husband, Owen (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau), returns after five years on the run. Hannah (Garner) and her stepdaughter Bailey (Angourie Rice) find themselves in a race, needing to figure out how to reunite their family before the past catches up to them. This picks up after the season 1 ending, which reveals that Owen is alive but in hiding. Along with Garner, Coster-Waldau, Rice, and Greer, The Last Thing He Told Me season 2 cast includes David Morse, Augusto Aguilera, Josh Hamilton, Nick Hargrove, Michael Galante, John Noble, Michael Hyatt, Luke Kirby, and Rita Wilson. Notable supporting actors from season 1, such as Criminal Minds star Aisha Tyler, are not mentioned, but they could potentially be making guest appearances. The Last Thing He Told Me is produced by 20th Television and Hello Sunshine, a part of Candle Media. It\'s executive produced by Dave, Singer, and Garner, as well as Hello Sunshine’s Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter. Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard also serve as executive producers alongside new co-showrunner Aaron Zelman. The next chapter in the saga of the Apple TV series, which sees Garner returning as executive producer, will have to contend with a promise Owen made to stay away from Bailey. That is potentially complicated by his direct encounter with Hannah. But it\'ll also have to deal with making the jump from limited series to ongoing drama. The Last Thing He Told Me season 1 made some book changes to better fit the screen. It will have to make some more adjustments, with the hope that Hannah\'s story is one that viewers will still be invested in after a break of almost three years. Based on the talent involved, the interest will likely still be there even after the hiatus. What\'s most interesting about this choice is that all of them, including main players Cooper Hoffman and David Jonsson , will be campaigning in the supporting acting categories across all the major awards circuits. This report comes exclusively from Variety , and its news that comes as surprising, but understandable. Overall, it\'s due to the magnitude of the film\'s story and how much it was reliant on the ensemble entirely rather than one actor. The Long Walk was released in September and was adapted by screenwriter JT Mollner from the novel of the same name written by Stephen King . The movie centers around teens who take part in a deadly contest where they have to keep walking or be shot on sight by the military if they fall under a certain speed. The movie was directed by Francis Lawrence, who is best known for directing several movies in The Hunger Games series of films. His transition to Stephen King\'s dystopian world was a huge success, with the film earning an 88% certified fresh rating on the review aggregate website Rotten Tomatoes. Part of what made The Long Walk such a successful film in the first place (and more than likely why Lionsgate is taking its interesting approach to awards season) is the chemistry between all the actors . While Hoffman and Jonsson are undeniably at the heart of the story, each individual character gets a moment to shine. The camaraderie among the walkers in the face of inevitable death is why The Long Walk is such a moving film. In \'The Long Walk,\' Every Cast Member is Essential Lionsgate Variety\'s report states that the creative team behind the film is firm in their belief that the premise and emotional investment hinges on every single actor working in unison . So, it only makes sense that all the main actors in the film, which includes the likes of Ben Wang, Garrett Wareing, Charlie Plummer, Tut Nyuot Jordan Gonzalez, and Joshua Odjick, will have a chance to be nominated. This plan will be reflected in any potential nominations at the Oscars, Golden Globes, Screen Actors Guild Awards, BAFTA, and the Independent Spirit Awards. The report also mentions that Judy Greer, who plays Hoffman\'s mother in the movie, will also be put forward in the supporting actress category of the aforementioned award ceremonies. 2025 has been a phenomenal year for Stephen King adaptations, with The Life of Chuck and The Running Man also being released this year. Each director behind the three King adaptations this year has brought their own distinct style to the stories, and The Long Walk stands out thanks to its brutality and timeliness. It will be interesting to see if any unexpected cast members get nominated for their work on the film outside of favorites like Hoffman or Jonsson. One aspect that will undoubtedly stand out is the final moments of several of the characters, as each actor brought raw emotion and intensity that made the stakes feel real. For a half century now, the author has found his novels and short stories adapted for both the big and small screen. 50 years is a long time, and they have shown great advances in the craft of filmmaking, but what remains steady is how adaptations have well-drawn characters to work with. How convincingly the projects are able to bring the stories’ supernatural elements to life is secondary to them. But, with the release of Edgar Wright’s The Running Man , the second adaptation of King’s 1982 novel, there has never been a better time to ask, “Can second cinematic takes on a King novel work better than the first time?” As one might expect, the results have varied. Videos by ComicBook.com What follows are the five big screen movies that were the second attempt to bring a King work to life. The film could have been a remake of a miniseries, but the remake must have gone to theaters. For instance, Salem’s Lot (2024) didn’t count because it debuted on HBO Max. How does The Running Man stack up against its sophomore effort brethren? Let’s find out. 5) Firestarter image courtesy of universal pictures Keith Thomas’ 2022 version of Firestarter was widely deemed inferior to the 1984 original, which wasn’t even a remotely high bar to clear. But that consensus is fair, as it’s a bland and not particularly visually appealing remake. Of all the more modern Stephen King movies, Firestarter feels the most loss. Everyone involved seems to know they’re in a wholly generic work and none of them seem to be giving it their all. The Razzie nomination for young Ryan Kiera Armstrong was out of line , but this is definitely a movie worthy of receiving some not so desirable Razzie love. Stream Firestarter on Netflix. 4) Carrie image courtesy of sony pictures releasing Unlike Firestarter , Carrie (2013) did have a high bar to clear in Brian De Palma’s 1976 classic, the very first cinematic adaptation of King’s works. And, while it does fall short in every regard, there are worse things Carrie could have been than wholly average. Chloë Grace Moretz tries, but she seems a bit miscast. Then there’s Julianne Moore, who overacts not unlike Piper Laurie did in De Palma’s film, but that was a particular tightrope Laurie walked to a much more successful degree. For the most part the movie just seems to exist to cash in on a brand name and make some swift and easy money for Sony on a relatively low-risk $30 million budget. All that said, it does have two performances that rival the work seen in the original film. Namely, Judy Greer was a great choice for the empathic Ms. Desjardin and Portia Doubleday is note perfect as the bullying Chris Hargensen. They steal the movie, but that’s not enough to make it good when most of the runtime is, of course, devoted to Carrie and Margaret White. Stream Carrie on fuboTV. Read Next The 10 Best Stephen King Adaptations by His Frequent Directors 3) Pet Sematary image courtesy of paramount pictures Technically, the 2019 version of Pet Sematary is better than Mary Lambert’s 1989 take . That film, which has a strong reputation it doesn’t quite deserve, is both self-serious and an utter cheese fest. It has what is undoubtedly the best screamed to the heavens “No!” in film history, including Darth Vader’s. The thing is, between the cheese of the screenplay and the charming performance by Fred Gwynne, the 1989 Pet Sematary is memorable. The 2019 version? It’s just dour and bland. That said, it is well-cast, with both Jason Clarke and Amy Seimetz struggling to inject some life into a film that seems to be trying to capitalize on It ‘s success two years prior. Stream Pet Sematary on Paramount+. 2) The Running Man image courtesy of paramount pictures Thanks to a charismatic lead performance by Glen Powell and typically stylish direction by Edgar Wright, The Running Man manages to stand above the 1987 Arnold Schwarzenegger fronted version even if it will likely escape the viewer’s memory shortly after the credits have rolled. Much to its credit it doesn’t take long to get going and, once it starts, it never stops. It’s a perfectly suitable and digestible popcorn movie, one that never quite goes as far as it should in its commentary about modern day society but gets points for trying, nonetheless. Perhaps most importantly, this is further proof after Anyone But You , Hit Man , and Twisters that Powell has exactly what it takes to carry a movie. 1) It & It Chapter Two image courtesy of warner bros. pictures As mentioned, we’re including movies that are more modernized versions of miniseries. However, it would be fair to debate just how much of an influence Tommy Lee Wallace’s 1990 It miniseries was on Andy Muschietti’s big screen duology. If anything, it was more inspired by another cinematic adaptation of King’s works: Stand by Me . Muschietti has stated that he wasn’t a big fan of the miniseries but, even still, that miniseries (which is structurally non-chronological, just like King’s book) existed before It and It Chapter Two , so we’re including them. And, while It Chapter Two is a major step down from its predecessor, it’s still good enough to help the duology secure the number one spot. From the work by the young cast to the tone to Bill Skarsgård’s performance as Pennywise it was an example of a lot of integral factors coming together just right. Directed by Dallas Jenkins (the multi-hyphenate filmmaker behind the TV series The Chosen ), this funny and moving film was released theatrically in November 2024. Lionsgate is releasing a Blu-ray/DVD/Digital HD combo pack just in time for this year’s festivities. The story centers on two families. Matriarch of the comfortably middle-class Bradley family, Grace (Judy Greer), has volunteered to direct their town church’s annual Christmas pageant. The woman usually in charge is sidelined due to injury. Grace and her husband Bob (Pete Holmes), along with their children Beth (Molly Belle Wright) and Charlie (Sebastian Billingsley-Rodriguez), aren’t nearly as judgmental as many of the families who attend their church. In fact, some of the other mothers believe Grace isn’t up to the task of spearheading the production. Things only become more contentious when the six Herdman kids, hellions who don’t normally attend church, decide to attend Sunday school (for the free snacks). Upon learning about the upcoming pageant, the six unruly Herdmans sign up for parts. The eldest, Imogene (Beatrice Schneider), wants to portray Mother Mary. Most of the snooty parishioners urge Grace to bar the Herdmans, universally considered to be the town hooligans (their parents remain unseen throughout), from participation. Even openminded Beth (who, in adult form—voiced by Lauren Graham—narrates the picture) is initially skeptical about the Herdmans’ ability to behave appropriately. The class struggle, middle versus lower, is central to this tale. Turns out Bob knows where the Herdman kids live as he has been delivering a Christmas ham to their residence for years. Taken aback by this revelation, and dismayed by their living conditions, Grace begins to believe in the Herdman kids’ apparent convictions. Imogene convinces her siblings to conduct deep research into the Christmas story to hopefully inject some gritty realism into the pageant. To reveal much more would risk spoiling the film’s considerable charms. Suffice it to say, things unfold in a far more nuanced way than one might suspect of a crowd-pleasing holiday comedy. It’s more of a drama, and the efforts by both families (the Bradleys’ growing realization that goodness and virtue exist outside of the bourgeoisie; the Herdmans’ discovery of a sense of personal pride) provide a genuine heart and soul to what could’ve easily been a silly romp. Have the tissues nearby (but also know, this isn’t a tragedy). Lionsgate’s Blu-ray edition includes a handful of bonus features. Director Dallas Jenkins is joined by producer Kevin Downes for an audio commentary track. A quintet of short featurettes offers some standard behind-the-scenes footage. Bloopers and deleted scenes round out the package. The Best Christmas Pageant Ever , well-acted (especially by Beatrice Schneider as the Herdmans’ de facto “mother” figure, Imogene) deserves recognition as a new holiday classic. news_text_raw_parsed: ["Deadline Print Article deadline-logo-svg Print ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Season 2 Sets Premiere Date At Apple TV With First-Look Photos At Rita Wilson & Judy Greer By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About ‘Percy Jackson And The Olympians’ Season 2 So Far ‘Zootopia 2’ Review: Disney Sequel Herds Familiar Themes While Successfully Expanding Animated Animal World From Metallica To Kate Bush, ‘Stranger Things’ Biggest Musical Moments Weave Into Spotify Experience Ahead Of Season 5 Launch View All November 5, 2025 7:00am L-R: Angourie Rice and Jennifer Garner in 'The Last Thing He Told Me' Season 2 Apple TV The Last Thing He Told Me Season 2 will return to Apple TV next year, and Rita Wilson has joined the cast for the next installment. The second season of the drama series, based on Laura Dave’s forthcoming sequel novel The First Time I Saw Him , will premiere Friday, February 20, 2026. There will be eight episodes. Related Stories News Everything We Know About ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Season 2 Casting ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’ Casts Judy Greer For Season 2 Season 2 will pick up as Owen Michaels (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau) shows up after five years on the run, initiating a race for Hannah Hall (Jennifer Garner) and her stepdaughter Bailey (Angourie Rice) to reunite their family “before the past catches up to them,” as the logline teases. The First Time I Saw Him will publish January 6, 2026, providing a hint at what’s to come for Hannah, Owen, Bailey and more ahead of the Season 2 premiere. Season 1 — which debuted in April 2023 — ended with Owen silently and subtly signaling to Hannah that he was still around by walking through her exhibition heavily disguised. Hannah had made a deal with Bailey’s grandfather Nicholas Bell (played by David Morse) that no harm would come to any of the three of them if Owen agreed to stay far away from Bailey. This is where Dave’s first novel, The Last Thing He Told Me , ended as well. RELATED: Jennifer Garner On ‘The Last Thing He Told Me’: “I Didn’t Think I Could Survive If Somebody Else Played The Role”; Author Laura Dave Hints Season 2 – Contenders TV Returning cast are Augusto Aguilera, Josh Hamilton, Nick Hargrove and Michael Hyatt. Newcomers in addition to Judy Greer, whose casting Deadline first announced , and Wilson include Michael Galante, John Noble, and Luke Kirby. Missing from the returners is Aisha Tyler, who played Hannah’s best friend Jules Nichols. Season 2 is executive produced by co-showrunners Josh Singer and Aaron Zelman alongside Hello Sunshine’s Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter. Star Garner also executive produces. Zelman joins Season 2 as co-showrunner. The Last Thing He Told Me is produced by 20th Television and Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine, a part of Candle Media. Created and adapted by Laura Dave, alongside Academy Award-winning co-creator Josh Singer, The Last Thing He Told Me was the first collaboration between the married Dave and Singer, who both serve as executive producers. Aaron Zelman, Daisy von Scherler Mayer and Merri D. Howard also serve as executive producers. Francis Lawrence’s “ The Long Walk ” will campaign its entire principal cast of boys — including Cooper Hoffman and David Jonsson — in the supporting acting categories across all major awards bodies, Variety has learned exclusively. The Lionsgate dystopian drama, adapted by JT Mollner from Stephen King’s early novel, hinges on the emotional dynamics among a group of teenage competitors forced to walk until only one remains. The filmmakers believe the film’s power lies not in traditional leads but in the collective experience — a choice they think is best reflected by submitting the ensemble together. Judy Greer, who plays a pivotal adult figure in the story, will also be campaigned in supporting actress races. Submitting the entire cast together highlights the filmmakers’ confidence in casting director Rich Delia, whose work stitching together a cohesive ensemble of emerging talent is expected to be a focal point of the campaign. The young actors deliver varied responses to the story’s brutal marathon. With its ensemble-driven structure and bold category placements, “The Long Walk” joins the growing trend of awards hopefuls challenging traditional definitions of lead and supporting roles. It became Apple\'s most-watched limited series since the streaming service\'s debut in 2019, speeding up talks for The Last Thing He Told Me season 2. Apple reveals that The Last Thing He Told Me season 2 will premiere on Friday, February 20, 2026, and will consist of eight episodes. Based on the upcoming novel The First Time I Saw Him by Laura Dave, the upcoming episodes pick up as Hannah\'s husband, Owen (Nikolaj Coster-Waldau), returns after five years on the run. Hannah (Garner) and her stepdaughter Bailey (Angourie Rice) find themselves in a race, needing to figure out how to reunite their family before the past catches up to them. This picks up after the season 1 ending, which reveals that Owen is alive but in hiding. Along with Garner, Coster-Waldau, Rice, and Greer, The Last Thing He Told Me season 2 cast includes David Morse, Augusto Aguilera, Josh Hamilton, Nick Hargrove, Michael Galante, John Noble, Michael Hyatt, Luke Kirby, and Rita Wilson. Notable supporting actors from season 1, such as Criminal Minds star Aisha Tyler, are not mentioned, but they could potentially be making guest appearances. The Last Thing He Told Me is produced by 20th Television and Hello Sunshine, a part of Candle Media. Howard also serve as executive producers alongside new co-showrunner Aaron Zelman. The next chapter in the saga of the Apple TV series, which sees Garner returning as executive producer, will have to contend with a promise Owen made to stay away from Bailey. The Last Thing He Told Me season 1 made some book changes to better fit the screen. What\'s most interesting about this choice is that all of them, including main players Cooper Hoffman and David Jonsson , will be campaigning in the supporting acting categories across all the major awards circuits. This report comes exclusively from Variety , and its news that comes as surprising, but understandable. Overall, it\'s due to the magnitude of the film\'s story and how much it was reliant on the ensemble entirely rather than one actor. The Long Walk was released in September and was adapted by screenwriter JT Mollner from the novel of the same name written by Stephen King . The movie centers around teens who take part in a deadly contest where they have to keep walking or be shot on sight by the military if they fall under a certain speed. The movie was directed by Francis Lawrence, who is best known for directing several movies in The Hunger Games series of films. His transition to Stephen King\'s dystopian world was a huge success, with the film earning an 88% certified fresh rating on the review aggregate website Rotten Tomatoes. Part of what made The Long Walk such a successful film in the first place (and more than likely why Lionsgate is taking its interesting approach to awards season) is the chemistry between all the actors . While Hoffman and Jonsson are undeniably at the heart of the story, each individual character gets a moment to shine. The camaraderie among the walkers in the face of inevitable death is why The Long Walk is such a moving film. In \'The Long Walk,\' Every Cast Member is Essential Lionsgate Variety\'s report states that the creative team behind the film is firm in their belief that the premise and emotional investment hinges on every single actor working in unison . So, it only makes sense that all the main actors in the film, which includes the likes of Ben Wang, Garrett Wareing, Charlie Plummer, Tut Nyuot Jordan Gonzalez, and Joshua Odjick, will have a chance to be nominated. This plan will be reflected in any potential nominations at the Oscars, Golden Globes, Screen Actors Guild Awards, BAFTA, and the Independent Spirit Awards. The report also mentions that Judy Greer, who plays Hoffman\'s mother in the movie, will also be put forward in the supporting actress category of the aforementioned award ceremonies. 2025 has been a phenomenal year for Stephen King adaptations, with The Life of Chuck and The Running Man also being released this year. Each director behind the three King adaptations this year has brought their own distinct style to the stories, and The Long Walk stands out thanks to its brutality and timeliness. It will be interesting to see if any unexpected cast members get nominated for their work on the film outside of favorites like Hoffman or Jonsson. One aspect that will undoubtedly stand out is the final moments of several of the characters, as each actor brought raw emotion and intensity that made the stakes feel real. For a half century now, the author has found his novels and short stories adapted for both the big and small screen. 50 years is a long time, and they have shown great advances in the craft of filmmaking, but what remains steady is how adaptations have well-drawn characters to work with. How convincingly the projects are able to bring the stories’ supernatural elements to life is secondary to them. But, with the release of Edgar Wright’s The Running Man , the second adaptation of King’s 1982 novel, there has never been a better time to ask, “Can second cinematic takes on a King novel work better than the first time?” As one might expect, the results have varied. Videos by ComicBook.com What follows are the five big screen movies that were the second attempt to bring a King work to life. The film could have been a remake of a miniseries, but the remake must have gone to theaters. For instance, Salem’s Lot (2024) didn’t count because it debuted on HBO Max. How does The Running Man stack up against its sophomore effort brethren? Let’s find out. 5) Firestarter image courtesy of universal pictures Keith Thomas’ 2022 version of Firestarter was widely deemed inferior to the 1984 original, which wasn’t even a remotely high bar to clear. But that consensus is fair, as it’s a bland and not particularly visually appealing remake. Of all the more modern Stephen King movies, Firestarter feels the most loss. Everyone involved seems to know they’re in a wholly generic work and none of them seem to be giving it their all. The Razzie nomination for young Ryan Kiera Armstrong was out of line , but this is definitely a movie worthy of receiving some not so desirable Razzie love. Stream Firestarter on Netflix. 4) Carrie image courtesy of sony pictures releasing Unlike Firestarter , Carrie (2013) did have a high bar to clear in Brian De Palma’s 1976 classic, the very first cinematic adaptation of King’s works. And, while it does fall short in every regard, there are worse things Carrie could have been than wholly average. Chloë Grace Moretz tries, but she seems a bit miscast. Then there’s Julianne Moore, who overacts not unlike Piper Laurie did in De Palma’s film, but that was a particular tightrope Laurie walked to a much more successful degree. For the most part the movie just seems to exist to cash in on a brand name and make some swift and easy money for Sony on a relatively low-risk $30 million budget. All that said, it does have two performances that rival the work seen in the original film. Namely, Judy Greer was a great choice for the empathic Ms. Desjardin and Portia Doubleday is note perfect as the bullying Chris Hargensen. They steal the movie, but that’s not enough to make it good when most of the runtime is, of course, devoted to Carrie and Margaret White. Stream Carrie on fuboTV. Read Next The 10 Best Stephen King Adaptations by His Frequent Directors 3) Pet Sematary image courtesy of paramount pictures Technically, the 2019 version of Pet Sematary is better than Mary Lambert’s 1989 take . That film, which has a strong reputation it doesn’t quite deserve, is both self-serious and an utter cheese fest. It has what is undoubtedly the best screamed to the heavens “No!” in film history, including Darth Vader’s. The thing is, between the cheese of the screenplay and the charming performance by Fred Gwynne, the 1989 Pet Sematary is memorable. The 2019 version? It’s just dour and bland. That said, it is well-cast, with both Jason Clarke and Amy Seimetz struggling to inject some life into a film that seems to be trying to capitalize on It ‘s success two years prior. Stream Pet Sematary on Paramount+. 2) The Running Man image courtesy of paramount pictures Thanks to a charismatic lead performance by Glen Powell and typically stylish direction by Edgar Wright, The Running Man manages to stand above the 1987 Arnold Schwarzenegger fronted version even if it will likely escape the viewer’s memory shortly after the credits have rolled. Much to its credit it doesn’t take long to get going and, once it starts, it never stops. It’s a perfectly suitable and digestible popcorn movie, one that never quite goes as far as it should in its commentary about modern day society but gets points for trying, nonetheless. Perhaps most importantly, this is further proof after Anyone But You , Hit Man , and Twisters that Powell has exactly what it takes to carry a movie. 1) It & It Chapter Two image courtesy of warner bros. pictures As mentioned, we’re including movies that are more modernized versions of miniseries. However, it would be fair to debate just how much of an influence Tommy Lee Wallace’s 1990 It miniseries was on Andy Muschietti’s big screen duology. If anything, it was more inspired by another cinematic adaptation of King’s works: Stand by Me . Muschietti has stated that he wasn’t a big fan of the miniseries but, even still, that miniseries (which is structurally non-chronological, just like King’s book) existed before It and It Chapter Two , so we’re including them. And, while It Chapter Two is a major step down from its predecessor, it’s still good enough to help the duology secure the number one spot. From the work by the young cast to the tone to Bill Skarsgård’s performance as Pennywise it was an example of a lot of integral factors coming together just right.
