With the sun setting down for the last time with The Summer I Turned Pretty , its European counterpart is just getting started with all the drama. Based on the book "Save You" by Mona Kasten , Maxton Hall follows fashion empire heir James Beaufort ( Damian Hardung ) and scholarship recipient Ruby Bell ( Harriet Herbig-Matten ) — both of whom are students at the elite Maxton Hall . When Ruby accidentally runs into a secret affair between student and teacher , James is pulled into the mess, igniting the spark to their would-be fiery relationship. But Maxton Hall isn\'t just about teen romance. Outside the school halls, the series talks about the class divide between James and Ruby\'s worlds . For James, being in a world of affluence comes with a cost — a price that James has to pay to his cutthroat, businessman father. Meanwhile, Ruby is determined to be the first in the family to enroll in college, and she\'s saving herself for the best: Oxford University. In the young adult genre, many stories similar to Ruby and James have been shared on the screen before. Without further ado, here are the shows to watch if you love Maxton Hall . 1 \'Gossip Girl\' (2007–2012) The cast of Gossip Girl posing around a car and looking at the camera. Image via The CW "XOXO, Gossip Girl." Television was never the same when Gossip Girl came to the screens. A show infamously referred to as "every parent\'s nightmare," the salacious series introduces the elite Upper East Siders , centering on ultimate IT girl Serena van der Woodsen ( Blake Lively ). Having vanished from the scene for a year, Serena returns to Manhattan, much to the chagrin of her on-and-off best friend Blair Waldorf ( Leighton Meester ). Much of the show is viewed through the overarching eye of the elusive Gossip Girl , a blogger who shares the overly personal woes of these wealthy kids. With the cream de la crème of New York City constantly stabbing each other in the back, there\'s always a scandal waiting to be revealed to the world. From trivial high school affairs to money embezzlement, nobody\'s safe from Gossip Girl . 2 \'Elite\' (2018–2024) Christian, Carla, and Polo in school uniforms looking at the camera in a promo photo for Élite. Image via Netflix Considered the modern, Spanish take on Gossip Girl , the equally wild and provocative Elite doesn\'t hold back on its shock factor . After their old school collapses, three working-class teens — Samuel ( Itzan Escamilla ), Nadia ( Mina El Hammani ), and Christian ( Miguel Herrán ) — receive scholarships to Spain\'s most exclusive school, Las Encinas. As they quickly learn, being book smart isn\'t enough to survive the cutthroat social hierarchy of their new school . What makes Elite different from Gossip Girl is its murder-driven mystery. Viewers have seen what having excessive money could do to someone\'s moral compass. But it\'s even more shocking when a teenager would actually kill a fellow student just to protect their reputation. As the privileged students are forced to face the consequences of their own actions, Elite is literally a crash course on class hypocrisy and corruption within school walls . 3 \'Cruel Intentions\' (2024) Sara Silva standing next to Sarah Catherine Hook in Cruel Intentions. Image via Prime Video An ode to the 1999 film , the reimagined Cruel Intentions follows step-siblings Caroline Merteuil ( Sarah Catherine Hook ) and Lucien Valmont ( Zac Burgess ), who dominate the Greek system at Manchester College, an elite university near Washington, D.C. When a hazing scandal threatens their power, they scheme to manipulate Annie Grover (Savannah Lee Smith), the U.S. Vice President\'s daughter, into joining their sorority . In this world of privilege, the art of seduction is just as powerful as monetary capital. Outside the show, it\'s a "hush-hush" secret that Greek life can be controversial. Cruel Intentions may have taken some creative liberties, but the reality isn\'t far from the truth. When a hazing incident leaves the son of a U.S. Congressman injured, Carolien and Lucien have no qualms about taking advantage of an innocent person just to keep their precious sorority running . These two peas in a pod will do anything to pay the price of power. 4 \'Young Royals\' (2021–2024) Two teenagers look sad and lean on each other, sitting alone in a room in \'Young Royals.\' Image via Netflix There\'s only so much the future king can bear, especially since he\'s just a teenager. Young Royals follows Prince Wilhelm of Sweden ( Edvin Ryding ), sent to an elite boarding school, Hillerska, after a public scandal. Struggling with royal expectations, he meets Simon ( Omar Rudberg ), a humble choirboy, and the two form a secret romance that challenges class boundaries and duty to the crown . When their relationship is exposed, Wilhelm must choose between love and obligation . Young Royals proves that being at the top can be an excruciatingly isolating experience. Wilhelm has everything lined up for him — the throne, status, and connections at the tip of his fingers. Yet, nothing emotionally fulfills him more than a genuine romance with somebody who couldn\'t care less about his reputation. But like most relationships between the rich and the poor, there will always be a deep class divide wedged between them . 5 \'The Buccaneers\' (2023–) Christina Hendricks and Kristine Froseth walk arm in arm outdoors in The Buccaneers Season 2. Image via Apple TV The Buccaneers follows a group of wealthy American women who travel to England to marry into the aristocracy . Amidst lavish parties and strict class divisions, Nan St. George ( Kristine Froseth ) faces a love triangle between the Duke of Tintagel ( Guy Remmers ) and his friend Guy ( Matthew Broome ) while uncovering secrets about her birth. Meanwhile, Conchita ( Alisha Boe ), Jinny ( Imogen Waterhouse ), and Honoria ( Mia Threapleton ) each battle scandal, abuse, and forbidden love in their pursuit of freedom, happiness, and self-worth . The Buccaneers show that happiness comes with a heavy price if you intend to be in the upper class. While it may not be the most representative of feminist takes (especially with the whole privileged nature of it all), it does show how women of the time disrupt, and sometimes fall victim to, the rigid expectations of aristocratic society . Their methods of survival may not be perfect given the circumstances, but their hearts are in the right places. 6 \'Gilmore Girls\' (2000–2007) Rory (Alexis Bledel) and Lorelai (Lauren Graham) in Gilmore Girls Image via The WB Just like Ruby, everyone dreams of going to an elite college after graduation . Gilmore Girls follows single mother Lorelai Gilmore ( Lauren Graham ) and her daughter in the charming town of Stars Hollow, Connecticut. A former runaway teen mom, Lorelai has grown to become a successful innkeeper. Her daughter Rory ( Alexis Bledel ), is a different story. With a penchant for academics, she\'s got her university options laid out for her, but her heart\'s set on Yale . Family is an important element in Maxton Hall , and so is in Gilmore Girls . Lorelai and Rory share a deep emotional bond as mother and daughter, but sometimes family members fight with each other, especially as Rory grows from a teenager to a young adult. Parallel to Ruby being obsessed with Oxford, Rory is just as determined to enter the best schools, setting her sights on one of America\'s top Ivy League colleges . 7 \'The O.C.\' (2003–2007) Mischa Barton as Marissa Cooper and Ben McKenzie as Ryan Atwood in The O.C. Image via FOX Life completely changes for Ryan Atwood ( Ben McKenzie ) in The O.C. a former troubled teen from Chino, his life turns 180 degrees after being taken in by public defender Sandy Cohen ( Peter Gallagher ) and his wealthy family in Newport Beach. Ryan befriends Sandy\'s son Seth ( Adam Brody ), forming a brotherly bond, and falls for Marissa Cooper ( Mischa Barton ), the girl next door with a messy family life. As Ryan adjusts to his new life and the privilege surrounding it, his past collides with the drama of Orange County. Fitting into a new school is an ordeal in itself. But when you\'re a transplant from the underprivileged to the upper class. Ryan may be gifted, but the moment he\'s put into the elite, he\'s torn between his rough upbringing and new opportunities. As he deals with a new environment, one that belittles him because of his former background, Ryan has to work twice as hard to prove he deserves a seat in Newport Beach . 8 \'Privileged\' (2008–2009) Lucy Hale as Rose with Ashley Newbrough as sister Sage and JoAnna Garcia Swisher in a promo for Privileged. Image via The CW Babysitting a bunch of grown rich girls can be hard work — that\'s the life of Megan Smith ( JoAnna Garcia ) in Privileged . The 23-year-old Yale graduate has big dreams in journalism. Unfortunately, they\'re put on hold after she\'s fired. Thanks to wealthy cosmetics mogul Laurel Limoges ( Anne Archer ), Megan is saved from unemployment. The only catch is that she has to tutor Laurel\'s spoiled twin granddaughters , Rose ( Lucy Hale ) and Sage ( Ashley Newbrough ). A forgotten CW gem , Privileged is a more bubbly and comedic take on the luxurious lifestyle . Despite being the older one, Megan is constantly the butt of the joke to the cheeky Baker twins. As a result, Megan literally treats them like children, starting with confiscating their cellphones (leading to a dramatic meltdown), to banning junk food. Viewers can\'t help but root for this struggling writer-turned-Palm Beach insider. 9 \'Bridgerton\' (2020–) The search for the next diamond of the season continues in Bridgerton . From the delicate art of courtships to the intimate moments in bed , Netflix\'s hottest London Regency era show follows the wealthy and influential Bridgerton family as each sibling tends to their respective romantic pursuits . Whether it\'s enemies-to-lovers Daphne Bridgerton ( Phoebe Dynevor ) and the Duke of Hastings ( Regé-Jean Page ), or former friends Colin Bridgerton ( Luke Newton ) and Penelope Featherington ( Nicola Coughlan ), the wedding bells ring almost every year. There are plenty more enemies-to-lovers tropes in Bridgerton where that came from. Throughout three seasons, the couples share one common thread: nobody expected these singles to end up married to each other. But that happy ending required some effort, including a fake courtship to pretend to be the town\'s salacious gossip columnist . Against all odds, opposites do truly attract. 10 \'One Tree Hill\' (2003–2012) \'One Tree Hill\' cast wearing vintage outfits and posing together in a Season 4 prom episode. Image via The CW One Tree Hill follows half-brothers Lucas ( Chad Michael Murray ) and Nathan Scott ( James Lafferty ), who share a passion for basketball and the same father but come from very different worlds. When Lucas joins Nathan\'s high school basketball team, they share an intense rivalry. Not only do they battle each other on the court, but also in their love lives . As these two high school boys grow up to become men , they\'ll learn to cope with adulthood, friendship, and forgiveness in the small town of Tree Hill. On top of the high school drama, One Tree Hill explores social hierarchy through Lucas\' clash with his wealthy half-brother Nathan after joining the elite basketball team. Much like James\' father in Maxton Hall , Lucas and Nathan\'s father, the manipulative businessman Dan Scott (Paul Johansson), isn\'t afraid of using his influence and power to shape his sons\' futures . Meanwhile, Karen ( Moira Kelly ), the single mother to Lucas and modest café owner, is the opposite of what Dan stands for, serving as a pillar of integrity in One Tree Hill . one-tree-hill-movie-poster.jpg Like Follow Followed One Tree Hill TV-14 Drama Romance Sports Release Date 2003 - 2012-00-00 Network The CW Cast See All Chad Michael Murray James Lafferty Hilarie Burton Paul Johansson Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming BUY Showrunner Mark Schwahn Genres Drama , Romance , Sports Seasons 9 Streaming Service(s) M Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. Henson To Star In Motivational New Netflix Drama ‘Tis So Sweet’ The Oscar-nominated actress teams up with Tyler Perry and DeVon Franklin for a moving true story about faith, healing, and second chances. Taraji P. Henson By Okla Jones · Updated October 30, 2025 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… Taraji P. Henson is stepping into one of her most heartfelt roles yet. The Academy Award–nominated actress will lead ’Tis So Sweet , an upcoming Netflix drama inspired by the true story of Lenore Lindsey, a Chicago bakery owner whose life changes after an extraordinary discovery forces her to confront the past and rediscover her faith, healing, and purpose. Set against the rich backdrop of the city’s South Side, this project promises to blend soulful storytelling with the emotional depth that has made Henson a staple in Black culture, and the film industry overall. of her generation. Tis So Sweet will be directed by Tasha Smith, adapted from a screenplay by Randy Brown ( Miracles From Heaven ). The film also stars recording artist, actor, and ESSENCE cover star Joey Bada$$, expanding the story’s emotional range with a multigenerational ensemble cast. Behind the scenes, DeVon Franklin and Tyler Perry will produce, with Tony Strickland and Angi Bones serving as executive producers for Tyler Perry Studios, alongside Bart Lipton. Tyler Perry, Photo by Prince Williams/ DeVon Franklin Courtesy of Netflix The film marks the second release from Tyler Perry and DeVon Franklin’s ongoing partnership with Netflix to create uplifting, faith-based stories for global audiences. Their first collaboration, Ruth & Boaz , reimagined a biblical tale in a modern Southern setting and quickly became a breakout hit, debuting at No. 2 on Netflix’s Global Top 10 Movies List. Production is expected to begin later this year, with Netflix set to release the film in 2026. TOPICS: Joey Bada$$ Netflix Taraji P. Henson To lead Peacock TV Show Based on 50 Cent Novel November 3, 2025 By Anubhav Chaudhry Peacock has reportedly added a new drama series led by Taraji P. Henson to its upcoming slate. The project is based on a recent novel by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and marks a collaboration between their production banners. Early details suggest it will blend crime, power, and moral conflict in a high-stakes story. Taraji P. Henson cast in Peacock’s TV show adaptation of 50 Cent novel Taraji P. Henson will star in and executive-produce Peacock’s television adaptation of The Accomplice, a crime novel by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and Aaron Philip Clark. The project, produced by Universal Content Productions, is currently in development with Jackson’s G-Unit Films and Television and Henson’s TPH Entertainment attached. No writer has been announced for the series (via Variety ). According to the official logline, Henson will play Nia Adams, a fearless Texas Ranger chasing master thief Desmond Bell. Henson, and made Three 6 Mafia Oscar winners. By Denton Davidson Plus icon Denton Davidson More stories by Denton ‘A Useful Ghost’: How a haunted vacuum cleaner became Thailand’s funniest (and most moving) awards contender 0 Comments Read more ‘The Voice of Hind Rajab’ drops trailer: Everything to know about Tunisia’s Gaza-set Oscar contender 0 Comments Read more Park Chan-wook on past Oscar snubs — and why ‘No Other Choice’ could be his golden invitation 0 Comments Read more November 10, 2025 8:00 am Taraji P. Henson, Paula Jai Parker, Terrence Howard, and Taryn Manning in Hustle & Flow Paramount/Courtesy Everett Collection Share Share on Facebook Post google Google Preferred Pin it Show more sharing options Share to Flipboard Post to Tumblr Submit to Reddit Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Email Print This Page 0 When Craig Brewer thinks back on Hustle & Flow, one word still comes to mind: miracle. “I’ve been thinking about what a miracle the movie is — that no one wanted to make it,” Brewer tells Gold Derby. “Rest his soul, John Singleton putting his house up for collateral, financing the movie for $2 million, and us just being out here in the Memphis heat making this movie with these newish actors — Terrence Howard , Taraji P. Henson , this new rapper on the scene, Ludacris . And somehow it all came together.” A movie no one wanted to make When Hustle & Flow premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival, it was the definition of an underdog story — a gritty, Memphis-made drama about a small-time hustler who dreams of becoming a rapper. Brewer remembers constant rejection before Singleton, a two-time Oscar nominee for Boyz n the Hood , decided to back the film himself. He knew about Three 6 Mafia , he knew what Southern rap was doing. He just got it.” Director Craig Brewer, producers Stephanie Allain, and John Singleton on set Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection That faith changed everything. The film went on to sell to Paramount in a $9 million distribution deal, earn two Oscar nominations, and deliver one of the most unforgettable Academy Award moments of the 2000s — when Three 6 Mafia won Best Original Song for “It’s Hard Out Here for a Pimp.” “Those guys didn’t have a touch of cynicism in them,” he says of rap group. “They stormed the stage in their street clothes, platinum grills shining, and just screamed with joy. Nobody was ready for that — but it was infectious.” After the ceremony, Brewer found himself at an after-party only Hollywood could produce. “I got invited to Prince ’s house,” he laughs. “There was a river of chocolate you could dip fruit into, Sheila E. was performing — it was absolutely wild. Ludacris grabbed me and said, ‘Do you know what this means for us? Three 6 Mafia just won an Academy Award.’ He was right. It was a big deal for the Southern rap scene.” Two stars are born For Brewer, one of the joys of revisiting Hustle & Flow two decades later is seeing how far his cast has come. The film marked a major turning point for both Terrence Howard and Taraji P. Henson, whose chemistry as DJay and Shug helped make the film a phenomenon. \'Hustle & Flow\': Terrence Howard, Taraji P. Henson Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection Both actors went on to become fixtures in Hollywood: Howard earned an Oscar nomination for Hustle & Flow and later starred in Empire, reuniting with Henson, who became one of television’s most commanding presences and earned her own Oscar nod for The Curious Case of Benjamin Button in 2009. Brewer even reconnected with them on last year\'s Peacock limited series Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist. “When Taraji got involved, I was so excited,” Brewer says. “But then Will Packer gave me a call and he’s like, ‘I don’t think we’re done. I think we need to go get your boy.’ I was like, ‘Are you really serious? You want me to go get Terrence?’ I remember calling up Terrence and saying, ‘All right, you know I love you. You know that I’m going to get out of your way and I’m going to give you everything that you want. I just want you to show up and give me everything you got.’” He laughs, recalling Howard’s unique on-set energy. “I’ll never forget him saying, ‘Well, I’ll tell you what I see. I see the Bee Gees. I want a Bee Gee wig.’ He had this long chestnut wavy wig that he just never wanted to take off. He wore it to the premiere.” Terrence Howard as Cadillac Richie in \'Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist\' Eli Joshua Adé/Peacock Still echoing through Memphis Two decades later, Hustle & Flow continues to reverberate across Brewer’s hometown. “You can’t go to a Memphis Grizzlies game without hearing 20,000 people chant ‘Whoop That Trick,’” he says proudly. “I’m talking old blue-haired ladies shouting it — and meaning it. It’s scary to the opposing team.” The chant, based on the film’s breakout anthem, has become a cultural calling card for Memphis — a symbol of pride, persistence, and scrappy energy. A family that never broke up The Hustle & Flow family, Brewer says, never really disbanded. “We’re all still very close,” he says. “ Al Kapone , who wrote ‘Whoop That Trick’ — everybody in Three 6 — we still all connect regularly. Elise Neal , who is in the movie, is a Memphis resident now. We hang out. Not only that, but there were strippers that were in our movie from 2005 that I had made my first movie with in 1999 ( The Poor & Hungry ). We go to kid birthdays and barbecues, and that’s just the way we do things here in Memphis. So, it’s a family that’s still together, I’m happy to say.” Singleton passed away in 2019, but Brewer still feels his presence. “I miss him a lot,” he says. “I wish he could have seen my next movie. I was really fortunate that he got to see an early cut of Dolemite Is My Name before he passed away. But Hustle & Flow is a special movie that has remained for a long time in people’s minds and the culture." How it connects to ‘Song Sung Blue’ Twenty years after Hustle & Flow, Brewer is once again returning to the world of dreamers and music with Song Sung Blue , his upcoming film starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson , opening Christmas Day. The film follows a working-class Milwaukee couple who perform in a Neil Diamond tribute band — and Brewer sees more than a few echoes between the two stories. “I hope everybody sees Song Sung Blue because it’s a little bit of a brother to Hustle & Flow, I feel,” he says. Kate Hudson and Hugh Jackman in Song Sung Blue Focus Features Both films, he explains, are about ordinary people trying to channel pain and hope into art. Where DJay built beats in a sweltering Memphis basement, Mike and Claire sing their hearts out under cheap stage lights — chasing something bigger than fame. “I love movies about people who are trying to start over,” Brewer says. “They not only want to do something different in their career and make this tribute band, but they also want to get married. They also want to see if they can start a family again after failure in that realm before.” The legacy For Brewer, Hustle & Flow remains a turning point that shaped both his life and career. The relationships forged on that set — from Singleton to the cast and crew he still calls family — continue to anchor his work two decades later. “It was a miracle the movie got made — and somehow, it all came together,” Brewer says . The film helped define his path as a filmmaker and strengthened his bond with the city that first believed in him. Obviously, not in real life. That\'s how birthdays, Christmases, and Thanksgivings end with a cake or turkey on the floor. However, in TV and film, those close interpersonal conflicts can breed some of the most dramatic and thrilling confrontations that have audiences begging for more. Just think about how Game of Thrones , Succession , and even Keeping Up With the Kardashians thrive off the battles, fictional or non-fictional, between those related by blood and outsiders who ruin that family dynamic. Well, if you are looking for a show that is every bit as wild and bingeable as those, look no further than Empire . This 5-season drama has almost everything a binge-watcher could ask for. Almost unbelievable plots, politicking, violence, sex, comedy, fantastic performances, and influential soundtracks. Not only did it help resurrect careers, but it showcased how the TV and music industries could interlink in real life, blurring two different kinds of artistry. With over 100 episodes to get through, Empire is a show that not only deserves your attention but will command it for weeks on end. \'Empire\' Follows the Lyon Family Hip-Hop Dynasty If someone were to ask how to describe Empire , the most succinct way possible would be that it was Succession before Succession . Perhaps not in terms of critical success, but certainly in terms of its premise. Empire follows the Lyon family as its patriarch, Lucious ( Terrence Howard ), decides who will take over the family business , the Empire music label that he built. Though, like Logan Roy ( Brian Cox ), he sees his options as limited. There is Andre ( Trai Byers ), who isn\'t musically talented like the other Lyons but acts as the consigliere of the family with his legal and business acumen; Jamal ( Jussie Smollett ), who feels like he was inspired by Pharrell Williams , though is looked down upon for his homosexuality by his father; and Hakeem ( Bryshere Y. Gray ), who is more interested in emulating his father\'s gangster background than acting like an adult. Among all of this is Cookie ( Taraji P. Henson ), Lucious\' ex-wife, who loves her children but also seeks to place herself as the one pulling the strings behind the scenes. With this, the stakes go beyond just business and familial relationships to attempted murder. Lines are crossed with complicated relationships that cross boundaries, as Lucious struggles to let go of his power and seeks to prove he is still the dominant force, even if he is not the one directly in control. Yet, under all the scheming and betrayals, there is still the heartache of each character loving their family and feeling they are forced to play this brutal game , with all the children really just wanting their father\'s approval. \'Empire\' Features Fantastic Performances and Revived Terrence Howard\'s Career Taraji P. Henson as Cookie Lyon in \'Empire\' Image via Fox With the almost over-the-top arcs these characters embark on, such as Hakeem stealing his own father\'s fiancée, Anika ( Grace Byers ), at one point, it would be easy for their performances to feel lacking in weight. However, this could not be further from the case. Despite the pair of them being mired in controversy and rightly condemned for some of their actions and words in recent years, it is impossible not to acknowledge how Smollett and Howard bring a necessary gravitas to their roles, especially with the complexity of their relationship as a gay son and a homophobic father . Empire was even credited with helping to revive Howard\'s career as a leading man following his departure from Marvel after Iron Man , even if the actor would go on to ruin his image again with further assault allegations and bogus pseudo-science claims. Posts 3 By Matt Goldberg Apr 29, 2010 However, the true star of Empire is undoubtedly Henson as Cookie, which won Henson a Golden Globe for "Best Performance by an Actress In A Television Series." Henson plays the character as witty yet also intensely petty and sometimes cruel, with one-liners such as summing up Hakeem\'s entire character with "You need to stop rappin\' like you from the streets, \'cause you not about that life!" or shutting down Lucious\' advances on her by saying "Get rid of fake-ass Halle Berry. As long as she\'s around, I\'m closed for business." With these lines, Henson doesn\'t just make the audience laugh with her sassy and snappy delivery, but plays a similar role to Cersei ( Lena Headey ) in later seasons of Game of Thrones , where there is something delightful about watching a woman outdo the men around her in a male-dominated world. She can even be unnecessarily blunt, telling Jamal that, "For a queen, you sure do keep a messy place. What you need is a good maid up in here." While a borderline homophobic thing to say, the context of Cookie\'s persona and love for her children keeps her sympathetic rather than making us hate her. \'Empire\' Changed How Music Was Viewed in TV Hakeem, Jamal, Cookie, and Lucious singing in the studio in Empire Image via FOX Being a show about musicians trying to take over a record label, Empire comes with some absolute bangers that are original songs from the actors that went far beyond the show\'s fanbase. In 2015, the Season 1 soundtrack hit #1 on the Billboard charts , the first to do so since Glee , which featured cover music . Incorporating this into the show, from boardrooms to recording booths, meant there was a versatility to Empire’s success and tone not often seen on today’s television. Some shows do attempt to replicate it, such as how The Witcher saw success with Joey Batey \'s recordings of songs like "Toss a Coin to Your Witcher," and "Burn Butcher Burn," which have over 100 million and 46 million streams on Spotify, respectively. But Empire paved the way for this kind of creative experimentation. While some may consider Empire to be a guilty pleasure, considering the dramatized nature of the characters and world they exist within, which sets it apart from the more grounded and nuanced world of Succession , there is no reason why you shouldn\'t embrace said pleasure. Cookie certainly wouldn\'t blame you. With some standout performances and trailblazing history, Empire isn\'t like many 5-season shows you\'ll watch, and that makes it all the juicier for your binge satisfaction. Taraji P. Henson By Okla Jones · Updated October 30, 2025 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… Taraji P. Henson is stepping into one of her most heartfelt roles yet. The Academy Award–nominated actress will lead ’Tis So Sweet , an upcoming Netflix drama inspired by the true story of Lenore Lindsey, a Chicago bakery owner whose life changes after an extraordinary discovery forces her to confront the past and rediscover her faith, healing, and purpose. Set against the rich backdrop of the city’s South Side, this project promises to blend soulful storytelling with the emotional depth that has made Henson a staple in Black culture, and the film industry overall. of her generation. Tis So Sweet will be directed by Tasha Smith, adapted from a screenplay by Randy Brown ( Miracles From Heaven ). The film also stars recording artist, actor, and ESSENCE cover star Joey Bada$$, expanding the story’s emotional range with a multigenerational ensemble cast. Behind the scenes, DeVon Franklin and Tyler Perry will produce, with Tony Strickland and Angi Bones serving as executive producers for Tyler Perry Studios, alongside Bart Lipton. Tyler Perry, Photo by Prince Williams/ DeVon Franklin Courtesy of Netflix The film marks the second release from Tyler Perry and DeVon Franklin’s ongoing partnership with Netflix to create uplifting, faith-based stories for global audiences. Their first collaboration, Ruth & Boaz , reimagined a biblical tale in a modern Southern setting and quickly became a breakout hit, debuting at No. 2 on Netflix’s Global Top 10 Movies List. Henson and co-hosted with her long time best friend Tracie Jade Jenkins, who is the Executive Director of Henson’s Boris Lawrence Henson Foundation . In the new original series, Golden Globe Award-Winning Actress Taraji P. Henson and Tracie Jade Jenkins will shine a spotlight on the challenging mental health issues facing us today – particularly of those in the Black community. Through personal interviews with both celebrities, experts and everyday people, the series will show how to provide support, bring awareness and help eliminate the stigmas of mental health issues. Each episode will focus on a different mental health topic with multiple content drops per week. Henson founded The Boris Lawrence Foundation in 2018, a nonprofit organization led by Tracie Jade Jenkins. The foundation is named in honor of Henson’s father, Boris Lawrence Henson, who suffered with mental health challenges as a result of his tour of duty in the Vietnam War. The organization is committed to changing the perception of mental illness in the Black community by encouraging those who suffer with this debilitating illness to get the help they need. Taraji P. Henson quote: “I’ve long been a mental health advocate for the Black community and created the Boris Lawrence Henson Foundation in 2018 that has provided resources to thousands of people who are struggling,” said Henson. “I’m looking forward to bringing this new talk series to Facebook Watch, where I can continue to create conversation around an issue that is near and dear to my heart.” See also Matt Bomer and Nathan Lane to Star in Hulu Series Mina Lefevre, Head of Development & Programming, Facebook Watch: “The work Taraji has done in the mental health space is inspiring, and we’re thrilled to have her come to our platform to educate and entertain around this incredibly important topic.” said Mina Lefevre, Head of Development & Programing for Facebook Watch. “One of our strengths at Facebook Watch is building community and conversation around topics people care about, and we’re looking forward to taking this journey together.” Peace of Mind with Taraji (WT) is the latest among a diverse slate of Facebook Watch talk shows, joining the critically acclaimed Red Table Talk with Jada Pinkett Smith , STEVE on Watch with Steve Harvey and Red TableTalk: The Estefans with Gloria Estefan premiering October 7. Brewer remembers constant rejection before Singleton, a two-time Oscar nominee for Boyz n the Hood , decided to back the film himself. He knew about Three 6 Mafia , he knew what Southern rap was doing. He just got it.” Director Craig Brewer, producers Stephanie Allain, and John Singleton on set Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection That faith changed everything. The film went on to sell to Paramount in a $9 million distribution deal, earn two Oscar nominations, and deliver one of the most unforgettable Academy Award moments of the 2000s — when Three 6 Mafia won Best Original Song for “It’s Hard Out Here for a Pimp.” “Those guys didn’t have a touch of cynicism in them,” he says of rap group. “They stormed the stage in their street clothes, platinum grills shining, and just screamed with joy. Nobody was ready for that — but it was infectious.” After the ceremony, Brewer found himself at an after-party only Hollywood could produce. “I got invited to Prince ’s house,” he laughs. “There was a river of chocolate you could dip fruit into, Sheila E. was performing — it was absolutely wild. Ludacris grabbed me and said, ‘Do you know what this means for us? Three 6 Mafia just won an Academy Award.’ He was right. It was a big deal for the Southern rap scene.” Two stars are born For Brewer, one of the joys of revisiting Hustle & Flow two decades later is seeing how far his cast has come. The film marked a major turning point for both Terrence Howard and Taraji P. Henson, whose chemistry as DJay and Shug helped make the film a phenomenon. \'Hustle & Flow\': Terrence Howard, Taraji P. Henson Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection Both actors went on to become fixtures in Hollywood: Howard earned an Oscar nomination for Hustle & Flow and later starred in Empire, reuniting with Henson, who became one of television’s most commanding presences and earned her own Oscar nod for The Curious Case of Benjamin Button in 2009. Brewer even reconnected with them on last year\'s Peacock limited series Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist. “When Taraji got involved, I was so excited,” Brewer says. “But then Will Packer gave me a call and he’s like, ‘I don’t think we’re done. I think we need to go get your boy.’ I was like, ‘Are you really serious? You want me to go get Terrence?’ I remember calling up Terrence and saying, ‘All right, you know I love you. You know that I’m going to get out of your way and I’m going to give you everything that you want. I just want you to show up and give me everything you got.’” He laughs, recalling Howard’s unique on-set energy. “I’ll never forget him saying, ‘Well, I’ll tell you what I see. I see the Bee Gees. I want a Bee Gee wig.’ He had this long chestnut wavy wig that he just never wanted to take off. He wore it to the premiere.” Terrence Howard as Cadillac Richie in \'Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist\' Eli Joshua Adé/Peacock Still echoing through Memphis Two decades later, Hustle & Flow continues to reverberate across Brewer’s hometown. “You can’t go to a Memphis Grizzlies game without hearing 20,000 people chant ‘Whoop That Trick,’” he says proudly. “I’m talking old blue-haired ladies shouting it — and meaning it. It’s scary to the opposing team.” The chant, based on the film’s breakout anthem, has become a cultural calling card for Memphis — a symbol of pride, persistence, and scrappy energy. A family that never broke up The Hustle & Flow family, Brewer says, never really disbanded. “We’re all still very close,” he says. “ Al Kapone , who wrote ‘Whoop That Trick’ — everybody in Three 6 — we still all connect regularly. Elise Neal , who is in the movie, is a Memphis resident now. We hang out. Not only that, but there were strippers that were in our movie from 2005 that I had made my first movie with in 1999 ( The Poor & Hungry ). We go to kid birthdays and barbecues, and that’s just the way we do things here in Memphis. So, it’s a family that’s still together, I’m happy to say.” Singleton passed away in 2019, but Brewer still feels his presence. “I miss him a lot,” he says. “I wish he could have seen my next movie. I was really fortunate that he got to see an early cut of Dolemite Is My Name before he passed away. But Hustle & Flow is a special movie that has remained for a long time in people’s minds and the culture." How it connects to ‘Song Sung Blue’ Twenty years after Hustle & Flow, Brewer is once again returning to the world of dreamers and music with Song Sung Blue , his upcoming film starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson , opening Christmas Day. The film follows a working-class Milwaukee couple who perform in a Neil Diamond tribute band — and Brewer sees more than a few echoes between the two stories. “I hope everybody sees Song Sung Blue because it’s a little bit of a brother to Hustle & Flow, I feel,” he says. Kate Hudson and Hugh Jackman in Song Sung Blue Focus Features Both films, he explains, are about ordinary people trying to channel pain and hope into art. Where DJay built beats in a sweltering Memphis basement, Mike and Claire sing their hearts out under cheap stage lights — chasing something bigger than fame. “I love movies about people who are trying to start over,” Brewer says. “They not only want to do something different in their career and make this tribute band, but they also want to get married. They also want to see if they can start a family again after failure in that realm before.” The legacy For Brewer, Hustle & Flow remains a turning point that shaped both his life and career. The relationships forged on that set — from Singleton to the cast and crew he still calls family — continue to anchor his work two decades later. “It was a miracle the movie got made — and somehow, it all came together,” Brewer says . The film helped define his path as a filmmaker and strengthened his bond with the city that first believed in him. Memphis still chants the film’s anthem at basketball games, and Brewer still calls its people his creative home. Read More: Craig Brewer FYC Hustle & Flow Paramount Song Sung Blue Taraji P. Obviously, not in real life. That\'s how birthdays, Christmases, and Thanksgivings end with a cake or turkey on the floor. However, in TV and film, those close interpersonal conflicts can breed some of the most dramatic and thrilling confrontations that have audiences begging for more. Just think about how Game of Thrones , Succession , and even Keeping Up With the Kardashians thrive off the battles, fictional or non-fictional, between those related by blood and outsiders who ruin that family dynamic. Well, if you are looking for a show that is every bit as wild and bingeable as those, look no further than Empire . This 5-season drama has almost everything a binge-watcher could ask for. Almost unbelievable plots, politicking, violence, sex, comedy, fantastic performances, and influential soundtracks. Not only did it help resurrect careers, but it showcased how the TV and music industries could interlink in real life, blurring two different kinds of artistry. With over 100 episodes to get through, Empire is a show that not only deserves your attention but will command it for weeks on end. \'Empire\' Follows the Lyon Family Hip-Hop Dynasty If someone were to ask how to describe Empire , the most succinct way possible would be that it was Succession before Succession . Perhaps not in terms of critical success, but certainly in terms of its premise. Empire follows the Lyon family as its patriarch, Lucious ( Terrence Howard ), decides who will take over the family business , the Empire music label that he built. Though, like Logan Roy ( Brian Cox ), he sees his options as limited. There is Andre ( Trai Byers ), who isn\'t musically talented like the other Lyons but acts as the consigliere of the family with his legal and business acumen; Jamal ( Jussie Smollett ), who feels like he was inspired by Pharrell Williams , though is looked down upon for his homosexuality by his father; and Hakeem ( Bryshere Y. Gray ), who is more interested in emulating his father\'s gangster background than acting like an adult. Among all of this is Cookie ( Taraji P. Henson ), Lucious\' ex-wife, who loves her children but also seeks to place herself as the one pulling the strings behind the scenes. With this, the stakes go beyond just business and familial relationships to attempted murder. Lines are crossed with complicated relationships that cross boundaries, as Lucious struggles to let go of his power and seeks to prove he is still the dominant force, even if he is not the one directly in control. Yet, under all the scheming and betrayals, there is still the heartache of each character loving their family and feeling they are forced to play this brutal game , with all the children really just wanting their father\'s approval. \'Empire\' Features Fantastic Performances and Revived Terrence Howard\'s Career Taraji P. Henson as Cookie Lyon in \'Empire\' Image via Fox With the almost over-the-top arcs these characters embark on, such as Hakeem stealing his own father\'s fiancée, Anika ( Grace Byers ), at one point, it would be easy for their performances to feel lacking in weight. However, this could not be further from the case. Despite the pair of them being mired in controversy and rightly condemned for some of their actions and words in recent years, it is impossible not to acknowledge how Smollett and Howard bring a necessary gravitas to their roles, especially with the complexity of their relationship as a gay son and a homophobic father . Empire was even credited with helping to revive Howard\'s career as a leading man following his departure from Marvel after Iron Man , even if the actor would go on to ruin his image again with further assault allegations and bogus pseudo-science claims. Posts 3 By Matt Goldberg Apr 29, 2010 However, the true star of Empire is undoubtedly Henson as Cookie, which won Henson a Golden Globe for "Best Performance by an Actress In A Television Series." Henson plays the character as witty yet also intensely petty and sometimes cruel, with one-liners such as summing up Hakeem\'s entire character with "You need to stop rappin\' like you from the streets, \'cause you not about that life!" or shutting down Lucious\' advances on her by saying "Get rid of fake-ass Halle Berry. As long as she\'s around, I\'m closed for business." With these lines, Henson doesn\'t just make the audience laugh with her sassy and snappy delivery, but plays a similar role to Cersei ( Lena Headey ) in later seasons of Game of Thrones , where there is something delightful about watching a woman outdo the men around her in a male-dominated world. She can even be unnecessarily blunt, telling Jamal that, "For a queen, you sure do keep a messy place. What you need is a good maid up in here." While a borderline homophobic thing to say, the context of Cookie\'s persona and love for her children keeps her sympathetic rather than making us hate her. \'Empire\' Changed How Music Was Viewed in TV Hakeem, Jamal, Cookie, and Lucious singing in the studio in Empire Image via FOX Being a show about musicians trying to take over a record label, Empire comes with some absolute bangers that are original songs from the actors that went far beyond the show\'s fanbase. In 2015, the Season 1 soundtrack hit #1 on the Billboard charts , the first to do so since Glee , which featured cover music . Incorporating this into the show, from boardrooms to recording booths, meant there was a versatility to Empire’s success and tone not often seen on today’s television. Some shows do attempt to replicate it, such as how The Witcher saw success with Joey Batey \'s recordings of songs like "Toss a Coin to Your Witcher," and "Burn Butcher Burn," which have over 100 million and 46 million streams on Spotify, respectively. But Empire paved the way for this kind of creative experimentation. While some may consider Empire to be a guilty pleasure, considering the dramatized nature of the characters and world they exist within, which sets it apart from the more grounded and nuanced world of Succession , there is no reason why you shouldn\'t embrace said pleasure. Cookie certainly wouldn\'t blame you. With some standout performances and trailblazing history, Empire isn\'t like many 5-season shows you\'ll watch, and that makes it all the juicier for your binge satisfaction. She is obsessed with all things TV, from anime and romantic fantasy to action-packed series. With that deep affection, Jiminna longs to share her excitement with all her readers through the Collider platform as a TV author. Through her writing she has created stories and blog posts of amazing book recommendations, showcasing her love of writing. Jiminna's goal is to inspire others to discover and embrace their love of stories in all of its forms. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Epic films have an incredible ability: they hook viewers into their realm of brilliance within the very first few minutes, and don't let go until the screen goes dark . Whether it's universe-shifting stakes or quality character arcs, quite a few movies have earned the status of being the greatest from start to finish, delivering cinematic journeys that are remembered long after the credits roll. A few epic triumphs are films like Gladiator , which immerses its viewers in the rich ancient world of Rome, and Spider-Man: No Way Home , which reshapes a hero’s journey in unexpected ways. They may be two vastly different cinematic experiences, but both stand as quality epic films. On this list are some of the most epic movies to hit the screens—experiences crafted for viewers' pleasure that genuinely grip them from beginning to end . 10 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon' (2000) Yu Shu Lien brandishes her jian sword Image via Sony Pictures Classics Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is a wuxia gem that introduced the genre to a global mainstream audience. The 2000s fantasy film follows renowned swordsman Li Mu Bai ( Chow Yun-Fat ), who has made the decision to retire and entrusts his legendary sword, the Green Destiny, to his friend . In a twist of fate, the sword is stolen by the willful aristocratic daughter of a governor, Jen ( Zhang Ziyi ), who has been secretly honing her martial skills. Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is a universally acclaimed masterpiece that not only earned itself 40 awards worldwide but is also praised for some of the best action sequences seen to date. The martial arts scenes are visually pleasing as they unfold like epic, dance-like sequences of graceful yet intense violent combat all throughout its run. From the film's gorgeous cinematography of China’s landscapes to its intimate story of duty, love, and freedom, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is an epic movie that remains one of the most beautiful and influential watches from beginning to end. 9 'Spirited Away' (2001) Chihiro standing among flowers and looking up in 'Spirited Away'. Image via Studio Ghibli This enticing fantasy film is often hailed as one of the greatest animated movies of all time . Spirited Away centers around 10-year-old Chihiro ( Rumi Hiiragi ), who winds up in a mysterious spirit realm and is forced into servitude by a cunning witch named Yubaba ( Mari Natsuki ), in order to survive and free her parents, who have been transformed into pigs. The anime epic took both children and adults on a journey of pure imagination and wonder. Its impact pushed the world to pay far more attention to the anime genre, as the movie stunned audiences so thoroughly with its universal themes of courage and friendship, and incredibly beautiful hand-drawn animation. Throughout the entire film, Spirited Away catapults its viewers into an extremely immersive and transformative adventure that feels much larger than its actual runtime, making it the ideal pick for this list of epic films. 8 'Titanic' (1997) Kate Winslet as Rose looks over Leonardo DiCaprio's shoulder at a drawing in Titanic. Image via 20th Century Studios Titanic is as epic as they come, standing as a highly beloved and devotedly cherished romance film . The movie, set in 1912, follows 17-year-old Rose DeWitt Bukater ( Kate Winslet ) as she boards the RMS Titanic as a first-class passenger with her stunningly wealthy family and boastful fiancé. Suffocating and suffering in a loveless relationship, Rose's contemplation of suicide halts as she encounters the dashing third-class passenger Jack Dawson ( Leonardo DiCaprio ). Titanic is a timeless gem of love and wonder that spans three incredible hours and is worth every minute of it. It stands now as more than a blockbuster hit—it's an undeniable cinematic phenomenon that wields a sweeping romance for the ages. Not one moment of the film is dull or falters in quality; for audiences, every minute is spent in Titanic's hypnotic blend of personal romance and historical tragedy. Titanic is an emotional journey that’s capable of thoroughly sweeping its audiences away from start to finish—a reminder that even love can outlive death. 7 'Gladiator' (2000) Russell Crowe looking upset in a tunic in Gladiator Image via Universal Pictures This Roman epic is a true tale of “sword-and-sandal.” The film Gladiator is set in 180 AD and centers around the respected general, Maximus Decimus Meridius ( Russell Crowe ), who, after a petty betrayal at the hands of the ambitious and cruel Commodus ( Joaquin Phoenix ) , is forced into slavery as a gladiator. Gladiator is an Oscar-worthy drama that delivers a crowd-pleasing spectacle in the best way. From its opening battles to its opulent arenas of Rome, Gladiator brought to life an epic and ancient world during its premiere, captivating its audience in a world of unmatched intensity for its entire runtime. Gladiator still remains an epic watch rife with rich storytelling, lavish production, and a larger-than-life atmosphere—a true modern historical classic that is the epitome of the epic movie experience. 6 'Spider-Man: Across The Spider-Verse' (2023) Miguel pins down Miles as he tries to escape the Spiderverse in Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse. Image via Sony Pictures Releasing Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is the second movie in the Miles Morales ( Shameik Moore ), Spider-Man films . The incredibly epic animated movie continues Miles' journey as a more mature superhero, who unexpectedly encounters a seemingly low-level villain called The Spot ( Jason Schwartzman )—only for that encounter to spiral into a multiversal crisis that threatens multiple universes and Miles’ happiness. After the hit movie Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse , quite a few fans believed that the story couldn’t get any better-and boy, were they mistaken . Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse not only delivers brilliant animated battles but also an unexpected emotional depth that elevates the film’s story by leaps and bounds. Audiences have frequently sung the movie’s praises, lauding it as one of the most dazzlingly bold and emotionally rich watches made in some time. With high, immersive stakes, creative multiverse storytelling, and a soundtrack worth talking about , Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse gifts audiences an incredible cinematic journey—one that has been consistently hailed as the greatest animated film of the decade, and is worth every minute of its runtime. 5 'Zack Snyder's Justice League' (2021) zack-snyders-justice-league-david-thewlis-ares-darkseid Image via HBO Max This iconic director’s cut is one of the best things to make it out of the 2021 cinematic universe . Zack Snyder’s Justice League delivers the complete four-hour vision that expands the film’s 2017 theatrical cut, following the death of the beloved hero Superman ( Henry Cavill ). With Earth truly vulnerable, the ancient evil, Steppenwolf ( Ciarán Hinds ), arrives to recover three Mother Boxes, with intentions of conquering Earth for the malicious, power-seeker monster, Darkseid ( Ray Porter ). The Snyder Cut is one of the biggest film turnarounds seen in cinematic history. The film, four hours long, has been lauded as one of the most unexpectedly entertaining superhero watches to make it onto screens—enhancing what was once only a potentially fantastic story through its extended reveals. From the movie’s rich operatic tone and mythic cinematography to the film’s epic fight sequences, Zack Snyder’s Justice League is a monumental and unforgettable experience from start to finish. 4 'Avatar' (2009) Neytiri and Jake in a Pandora forest in Avatar 2009 Image via 20th Century Studios Avatar is a true storm of epic proportions in the cinematic universe . The worldwide phenomenon is set in the mid-22nd century and centers around paralyzed former Marine, Jake Sully ( Sam Worthington ), who, due to his brother’s untimely death, is recruited to operate an “avatar”—a genetically engineered Na’vi-human hybrid—on the alien moon Pandora. From its incredible 3D technology to its emotional storytelling, Avatar stands as a timeless cinematic masterpiece for the ages. The film’s world-building is incredibly astonishing, while its action scenes are just as breathtaking —delivering absolute cinematic excellence for its entire runtime . With soaring scores and visuals quite literally able to stun its viewers, Avatar offers a perfect and extremely influential work of art that never falters in its high quality, from its opening scenes to its rolling credits. To date, the movie remains one of the highest-grossing films of all time, making it the ideal pick for this list of epic movies. 3 'Spider-Man: No Way Home' (2021) Tom Holland in his Spider-Man uniform with the mask off in Spider-Man: No Way Home. Image via Sony Pictures Releasing This movie masterpiece is one that artfully celebrates the treasured legacy of Spider-Man . Spider-Man: No Way Home follows the repercussions of Peter Parker's ( Tom Holland ) shocking unmasking. In a bid to return his life to the way it was, Peter seeks help from the time-altering Doctor Strange ( Benedict Cumberbatch ), only for things to go incredibly wrong, with the opening of the multiverse. No Way Home is the perfect homage to a strong legacy that has entertained millions for decades. The film skillfully blends fan service, nostalgia, and emotional storytelling—offering audiences a thrill ride from beginning to end . This epic superhero installment is one for the books, ultimately revealing that the entire trilogy is one long origin story for Holland’s Spider-Man. With a host of incredible action, iconic multiverse crossovers, and a story detailing the culmination of self-sacrifice, Spider-Man: No Way Home is an unforgettably epic experience that landed itself in the superhero film hall of fame. 2 'Avengers: Endgame' (2019) Robert Downey Jr. as Tony Stark / Iron Man snapping to end the battle in Avengers:Endgame Image via Marvel Studios Avengers: Endgame is a standing masterpiece of the superhero genre . The film, a culmination of the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s first grand saga, picks up five years after the heartbreaking events of Infinity War . Avengers: Endgame is the perfect ending to a saga of pure epicness. The movie’s three-hour runtime is filled with rich storytelling and unbelievable action from start to finish . The film shook the world as it became a true global cinematic event of an unprecedented scale, immediately after its premiere—highly praised for its narrative ambition rife with character and heart. With stunning battle sequences, a thrilling story, and brilliant production, Avengers: Endgame gifts audiences an emotionally satisfying climax that offers closure on beloved characters and years of amazing storytelling. 1 'The Dark Knight' (2008) Batman racing through the streets in The Dark Knight (2008) Image via Warner Bros. Pictures This genre-defining superhero epic is widely hailed as not only one of the best superhero films ever made, but one of the absolute best thrill rides from beginning to end . The Dark Knight follows the beloved vigilante of Gotham City, Bruce Wayne/Batman ( Christian Bale ), as he faces his greatest challenge yet—criminal mastermind, Joker ( Heath Ledger ). The Dark Knight transcended the superhero genre during its premiere and is now frequently regarded as a modern epic crime thriller that features some of the most treasured comic book characters. Heath Ledger’s performance alone can be considered one of the greatest portrayals seen in cinematic history—elevating an already standout film. From its consistent tension during its two-and-a-half-hour run to its iconic, award-winning performances, The Dark Knight stands as a groundbreaking masterpiece that features some of the most epic storytelling seen on the big screen. Searle Published 5 days ago Born with Autism (formerly classified as Asperger syndrome), Tyler B. Searle has been obsessed with storytelling since he was old enough to speak. He gravitated towards fairy tales, mythology, the fantasy genre, and animated movies and shows aimed at family audiences. When not writing, Tyler enjoys watching more cartoons and reading fantasy books in his home in Ontario, Canada. Sign in to your Collider account follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Fantasy is perhaps the most diverse and creative genre of storytelling because it allows us to make sense of the world around us and our emotions through symbolism and metaphors in the shape of everything from talking animals, valiant knights, fire-breathing dragons, and lands where magic and mystery abound. Fantasy allows us to confront the problems in our everyday lives by showing how they can be overcome in an out-of-this-world setting. Fantasy is also a very malleable genre; any story can be considered a fantasy if it has mystical and supernatural elements. Thus, it can also be paired with other genres, which can help encourage people who might normally overlook fantasy stories to give it a chance. Granted, there\'s nothing wrong with disliking a genre for one reason or another, but this aversion might be due to a lack of understanding of what fantasy actually is. This list includes several movies that best represent the genre , both high and low, both sweet and sorrowful. They encompass the genre\'s strongest elements and can make a believer out of those who dislike fantasy the most . \'Stardust\' (2007) Claire Danes and Charlie Cox looking stunned in a scene from Stardust. Image via Paramount Pictures Tristan Thron ( Charlie Cox ) is a young man living in the village of Wall on the edge of the magic kingdom of Stormhold, who longs to win the affection of a woman named Victoria ( Sienna Miller ). One night, they witness a star falling from the sky, and Tristan vows to retrieve it for her in exchange for her hand in marriage. However, the star has taken the form of a human woman named Yvaine ( Claire Danes ), and others are eager to claim her as well, such as a trio of witches who want to use her heart to regain their youth, and the princes of Stormhold, who want the ruby that knocked Yvaine from the sky in the first place. Stardust has quite a few differences from Neil Gaiman \'s novel that help make it a more casual and enjoyable movie. It does down a lot of the darker parts for a more lighthearted rom-com tone , allowing for quirky characters and a very cute romance between Thrstan and Yvaine. The acting also helps add to the charm, with Michelle Pfeiffer giving an enjoyable, wicked performance as the lead witch, Mark Strong beginning his villain career with the evil Prince Septimus, and Robert De Niro stealing the show as the crossdressing and cultured sky pirate, Captain Shakespeare. \'The Dark Crystal\' (1982) A sill image from the 1982 dark fantasy film, The Dark Crystal. Image via Universal Pictures Jen ( Stephen Garlick ) is one of the last Gelflings left on the planet Thra, and lives with the wise urRu, mystical ancients who hide from the tyrannical and decadent Skeksis who rule Thra. When their Master ( Brian Muehl ) dies, he tells Jen to seek out the wise woman Aughra ( Billie Whitelaw ) and retrieve a shard of the Dark Crystal that the Skeksis use to control Thra and extend their lives. If Jen can repair the crystal before the Great Conjunction of the world\'s three suns, he can save Thra and bring an end to Skeksis rule. Few movies reach the same level of immersion as The Dark Crystal . Thanks to masterful puppetry and a lack of human characters, the movie truly feels like you\'ve stepped into a world completely foreign to ours, where nearly everything is alive and active with unique movements. The Skeksis are the standout creatures in the film: they are highly expressive thanks to articulate facial features and flamboyant personalities, making them the perfect allegory for avarice, tyranny, and decadence. \'The Shape of Water\' (2017) Sally Hawkins as Elisa and Doug Jones as The Amphibian Man lock eyes through a tank in The Shape of Water. Image via Searchlight Pictures Elisa Esposito ( Sally Hawkins ) is a mute woman working at a secret government laboratory during the Cold War, whose only friends include her coworker Zelda ( Octavia Spencer ) and her neighbor, Giles ( Richard Jenkins ). One day, Colonel Richard Strickland ( Michael Shannon ) arrives at the lab with a revolutionary discovery: an amphibious humanoid ( Doug Jones ). As Strickland instructs his scientists to study the creature\'s respiratory system, Elisa enlists her friends to help free him, and she and the creature develop a romantic connection. The Shape of Water is Guillermo del Toro \'s hybridization of Creature from the Black Lagoon and Beauty and the Beast , resulting in one of the most unique romance stories in cinema . Its success comes from how the film deconstructs the idea of "the other" and society\'s habit of demonizing those who do not fit in with the accepted norm. Thus, the love that blooms between Elisa and the creature demonstrates the power of human empathy as those considered "others" can find solace in one another. \'Everything Everywhere All at Once\' (2022) Image via A24 Evelyn Quan Wang ( Michelle Yeoh ) is a struggling Chinese American who is juggling the IRS and an estranged relationship with her husband Waymond ( Ke Huy Quan ) and daughter Joy ( Stephanie Hsu ). One day, Evelyn learns about the multiverse, which is under threat of destruction due to the mysterious Jobu Tupaki. Evelyn gains the ability to hop into alternate versions of herself and access their memories and skills, which she uses to try and stop Jobu while trying to find fulfillment in her life choices. Everything Everywhere All at Once is a visually stunning movie that takes the audience on an absurdist multiversal journey that touches on powerful existential themes . Nihilism is a major theme here, using the multiverse and the concept of infinite choices to question whether anything in existence matters, and if so, what gives life meaning? The actors do a phenomenal job bringing their characters to life, particularly Yeoh, whose balance of comedic timing and emotional pathos anchors the film\'s emotional core. \'The Secret of Kells\' (2009) Brendan writing in a book with a quill while Aidan looks on in The Secret of Kells. Image via Buena Vista International Brendan ( Evan McGuire ) is a young boy living with his uncle, Cellach ( Brendan Gleeson ), the abbot of Kells, who is focused on building a wall to protect the abbey from invading Northmen. One day, they are visited by Brother Aidan ( Mick Lally ), a master illuminator who has come from the island of Iona with an unfinished manuscript. Since his age is impacting his ability to illuminate the book, Aidan recruits Brendan to help him, and Brendan also befriends a mysterious girl from the forest named Aisling ( Christen Mooney ). The Secret of Kells can best be summed up in one word: magical . Its stylistic animation and vibrant colors do a phenomenal job mimicking the style of a medieval illuminated manuscript come to life, and help to give the film a mystical quality that highlights the more fantastical elements of the story, especially Aisling. It\'s also not afraid to show off some dark imagery, especially when the Viking soldiers arrive, which helps remind us to enjoy the moments of beauty while they last. \'The Princess Bride\' (1987) Westley stands on guard with his sword while Buttercup stands behind him in The Princess Bride. Image via 20th Century Studios A grandfather ( Peter Falk ) reads a bedtime story to his sick grandson ( Fred Savage ). It follows a peasant woman named Buttercup ( Robin Wright ), who loses her love, Westley ( Cary Elwes ), while he is at sea, and is chosen by Prince Humperdinck ( Chris Sarandon ) to be his bride. However, Buttercup is abducted by a trio of bandits who hope to start a war with Humperdinck\'s enemies, but their attempts to flee with her are thwarted by a mysterious and highly skilled man in black. The Princess Bride was a commercial failure on release, but has since developed a large cult following that has elevated it to one of the best fantasy films ever made . It knows exactly what it is: a low-stakes film that embraces classic tropes and is full of heartfelt romance, exciting swordfights, and quirky dialogue . The cast is also a big reason for the film\'s likability, thanks to their great repertoire and ability to immerse themselves in the role, especially Mandy Patinkin as the Spanish fencer Inigo Montoya. \'Shrek\' (2001) Shrek in the first Shrek movie. Image via DreamWorks Animation When Lord Farquaad ( John Lithgow ) of Duloc banishes all fairy tale creatures from his land, they are forced into a swamp owned by an antisocial ogre named Shrek ( Mike Myers ). When Shrek confronts him about this, Farquaad agrees to remove the squatters if Shrek goes to a dragon-guarded castle to rescue his intended bride, Princess Fiona ( Cameron Diaz ). With the aid of a talking donkey ( Eddie Murphy ), Shrek agrees to the task, but discovers that there is a lot more to this princess than first appears. Shrek changed the world of animated films on release, and also ushered in a new era of fairy tale satire with its cynical jokes and less-than-appealing visuals. Over 20 years later, the film remains iconic thanks to the emotional weight behind its characters and story. When you get past the hilarious jokes and the jabs at Disney, Shrek is a movie about finding acceptance from yourself and others, as well as a reminder not to judge others before you get to know them. \'Pan\'s Labyrinth\' (2006) Image via Warner Bros. Pictures Ofelia ( Ivana Baquero ) is a young girl living in Francoist Spain, whose pregnant mother has recently married Captain Vidal ( Sergi López ), a staunch Falangist. One night, she follows a fairy into a subterranean labyrinth and meets a faun ( Doug Jones ), who tells her that she is the reincarnation of the princess of the underworld. To re-enter her kingdom, she must complete three dangerous tasks, all while still tending to her ill mother and avoiding Vidal\'s wrath as he ruthlessly hunts down Maquis rebels. Pan\'s Labyrinth is a masterpiece of dark fantasy that weaves its fantastical elements into the day-to-day struggles that Ofelia goes through in such a tumultuous period. The most obvious example is the Pale Man (Doug Jones), a decrepit creature that sits before a lavish feast. Rather than eat it himself, he uses it to lure children for him to devour, much like how vile regimes destroy their youth in the name of ideology. It also delves into dark themes of resistance and self-sacrifice , which lead to a beautifully bittersweet ending open to interpretation. \'The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring\' (2001) In the pleasant green land of the Shire, the hobbit Bilbo Baggins ( Sir Ian Holm ) vanishes during his 111th birthday party, and leaves all of his possessions to his nephew, Frodo ( Elijah Wood ). Among his inheritance is a magic gold ring that, unfortunately, is identified as the One Ring forged by the Dark Lord Sauron ( Alan Howard ), and within which is contained a great portion of his power and will to dominate. On the advice of the wizard Gandalf ( Sir Ian McKellen ), Frodo and three companions—his friend Samwise Gamgee ( Sean Aston ), and his cousins Meriadoc Brandybuck ( Dominic Monnaham ) and Peregrin Took ( Billy Boyd )—make for the elven city of Rivendell to seek council from Lord Elrond ( Hugo Weaving ), but the servants of Sauron are close at hand. The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring marks the beginning of Sir Peter Jackson \'s legendary film trilogy , which proved that fantasy movies had the punch to be epic blockbusters . It\'s all thanks to how masterfully it weaves together multiple film techniques and special effects, including specially designed sets to make the Hobbit characters look smaller than everyone else, gorgeous landscapes and map paintings that successfully transport the audience into a fantasy world , and great practical effects, costumes, and CGI to make the creatures feel alive. But it\'s the emotions of the story that truly hook you: the actors perfectly embody each of their characters, and as such, the weight of the mission and their individual friendships are felt fully. \'Spirited Away\' (2001) Chihiro holding into Haku as he flies above the river in Spirited Away Image via Studio Ghibli On the way to their new home, Chihiro ( Rumi Hiiragi/Daveigh Chase ) and her parents stumble into the spirit world and become trapped at sundown. Her parents are turned into pigs, but Chihiro is saved by a boy named Haku ( Miyu Irino/Jason Marsden ), who helps her get a job at the local bathhouse run by the witch Yubaba ( Mari Natsuki/Suzanne Pleshette ). If Chihiro wants to save her parents and get back home, she\'ll have to make friends with spirits who have a low view of humans and make sense of the world\'s strange laws and customs. Spirited Away is an animated masterpiece that combines the whimsical, otherworldly feeling of Alice\'s Adventures in Wonderland with Japanese Shintoism and fantastic characters. It\'s a classic coming-of-age story, with the spirit world and its various obstacles forcing Chihiro to rise to the occasion and mature while never losing sight of her virtues, like kindness and empathy. It\'s also an artistic marvel, with some of the most detailed animation ever put onto screen , and many moments of quiet atmosphere to let you sit in the scene\'s emotions and beauty. The 100 Greatest Movies Ever Made (And Where To Watch Them) 1) The Lord Of The Rings: The Fellowship Of The Ring (2001) Director: Peter Jackson Starring: Elijah Wood, Sean Astin, Ian McKellen, Viggo Mortensen, Orlando Bloom, Sean Bean, Cate Blanchett, Liv Tyler Release Date: December 13, 2001 Runtime: 178 minutes A wizard is never late. Nor is he early. He arrives precisely when he... well, you know the rest. It might have taken 20 years for New Zealand director Peter Jackson\'s plucky fantasy to clamber, Mount-Doom-style, to the very pinnacle of our greatest-movies pantheon. But here it is, brighter and more resplendent than ever. The Fellowship Of The Ring contains so much movie. Even at the halfway point, as the characters take a breather to bicker in Rivendell, you already feel sated, like you\'ve experienced more thrills, more suspense, more jollity and ethereal beauty than a regular film could possibly muster up. But Jackson is only getting started. Onwards his adventure hustles, to the bravura dungeoneering of Khazad-dum, to the sinisterly serene glades of Lothlorien, to the final requiem for flawed Boromir amidst autumnal leaves. As Fellowship thrums to its conclusion, finally applying the brakes with a last swell of Howard Shore\'s heavenly score, you\'re left feeling euphoric, bereft and hopeful, all at the same time. The Two Towers has the coolest battle. The Return Of The King boasts the most batshit, operatic spectacle. But Fellowship remains the most perfect of the three, matching every genius action beat with a soul-stirring emotional one, as its Middle-earth-traversing gang swells in size in the first act, then dwindles in the third. This oddball suicide squad has so much warmth and wit, they\'re not just believable as friends of each other — they\'ve come to feel like they\'re our buddies too. An ornately detailed masterwork with a huge, pulsing heart, it\'s just the right film for our times — full of craft, conviction and a belief that trudging forward, step by step, in dark days is the bravest act of all. Its ultimate heroes aren\'t the strongest, or those with the best one-liners, but the ones who just keep going. And so Fellowship endures: a miracle of storytelling, a feat of filmmaking and still the gold standard for cinematic experiences. Right, now that\'s decided, who\'s up for a second breakfast? The World (2010) Director: Edgar Wright Starring: Michael Cera, Mary Elizabeth Winstead, Chris Evans, Brie Larson, Jason Schwartzman, Anna Kendrick, Aubrey Plaza Release Date: August 13, 2010 Runtime: 112 minutes With Scott Pilgrim Vs. The World , Edgar Wright leaned all the way into the things that make his directorial style so singular — excellent needle drops, a poppy visual palette, whip-pans and whip-smart wit — in order to do Bryan Lee O\'Malley\'s graphic novels justice. Michael Cera is on peak socially-awkward-Cera form as the put-upon protagonist who\'s forced to face his new girlfriend\'s (Mary Elizabeth Winstead) seven evil exes in a series of increasingly wild face-offs. But it\'s the film\'s extraordinarily stacked ensemble (Chris Evans! Brie Larson! Anna Kendrick! Aubrey Plaza!), mixed-media aesthetics, and endless pool of iconic quotes and playlist-essential tunes that cement it as one of Wright\'s most memorable. This is good garlic bread. Streaming on: Apple TV Read Empire\'s review of Scott Pilgrim Vs. The World 95) Donnie Darko (2001) Director: Richard Kelly Starring: Jake Gyllenhaal, Jena Malone, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Patrick Swayze, Mary McDonnell Release Date: October 26, 2001 Runtime: 113 minutes A high school drama with a time-travelling, tangential universe-threading, sinister rabbit-featuring twist, Richard Kelly\'s labyrinthine opus was always destined for cult classic status. An early beneficiary of physical media\'s move to DVD, it gained a fandom in film obsessives who could pause, play, and skip back and forth through it at will. Any attempt to synopsise the movie is a fool\'s errand, but there\'s more than a hint of It\'s A Wonderful Life in the way we see Donnie (Jake Gyllenhaal, in a star-making turn) experiencing how the world would be worse off if he survives the jet engine that mysteriously crashes through his bedroom. That the film, with all its heavy themes and brooding atmosphere, manages to eventually land on a note of overwhelming optimism is a testament to Kelly\'s mercurial moviemaking. Streaming on: Prime Video | Hulu | Fubo TV Read Empire\'s review of Donnie Darko . 96) Brokeback Mountain (2005) Director: Ang Lee Starring: Heath Ledger, Jake Gyllenhaal, Anne Hathaway, Michelle Williams Release Date: December 9, 2005 Runtime: 134 minutes Ang Lee\'s adaptation of Annie Proulx\'s short story retains its source\'s sensitivity and grace whilst expanding its scope gorgeously. Played out against the beautiful mountain landscapes of Wyoming (in reality, the Canadian Rockies), the decades-spanning love story between shepherds Ennis Del Mar (Ledger) and Jack Twist (Gyllenhaal) — two men who unexpectedly find love, only to find it tested over the years as heteronormative expectations work against them — is sensually observed and immaculately shot. (No wonder it\'s in our list of the 50 greatest LGBTQ+ movies .) Delivering hope and heartbreak in equal measure, the multiple Oscar-winning movie\'s impact on queer cinema continues to be felt today. We still don\'t know how to quit it (and honestly, we don\'t want to). Rent on: Apple TV | Amazon Video Read Empire\'s review of Brokeback Mountain 97) Amélie (2001) Director: Jean-Pierre Jeunet Starring: Audrey Tautou, Mathieu Kassovitz, Rufus, Lorella Cravotta Release Date: April 25, 2001 Runtime: 122 minutes French director Jean-Pierre Jeunet\'s fourth feature – his second as a solo artist divorced from Marc Caro – saw the Delicatessen and Alien: Resurrection filmmaker leave behind the overwhelming darkness of his earlier works and step out into the glorious sunshine of Amélie \'s whimsical fantasy of Paris. Sure, a cynic could read the film as the story of Audrey Tautou\'s monomaniacal title character\'s relentless, somewhat stalkerish pursuit of the hapless Nino (Matthieu Kassovitz) around Montmartre\'s dream-like cityscape. But this one isn\'t for the cynics — it\'s a tribute to the daydreamers of this world, and a sweet, nostalgic, sentimental romantic comedy that only Jeunet could have conceived. Amélie will always be on our list of things we like. Rent on: Apple TV | Amazon Video Read Empire\'s review of Amelie 98) Paddington 2 (2017) Director: Paul King Starring: Ben Whishaw, Hugh Bonneville, Sally Hawkins, Hugh Grant, Brendan Gleeson Release Date: November 9, 2017 Runtime: 103 minutes With the first Paddington , co-writer/director Paul King delivered a truly wonderful, thoroughly British film bursting with joy, imagination, kindness, and just the odd hard stare from our beloved Peruvian bear. Then, he followed it by making one of the greatest sequels — nay, one of the best, most feel-good movies , period — of all time. Matching wits with Hugh Grant\'s moustache-twirlingly evil and deliciously outré washed-up actor Phoenix Buchanan, Paddington (Ben Whishaw) is on typically adorable form here as his search for a special present for his Great Aunt Lucy leads to all sorts of hilarious hijinks. Like all great sequels, this one takes everything that made the first so good and builds on it, dialling up the spectacle, the silliness, and the emotional stakes. And Harold Ramis, directing and co-writing with Danny Rubin, manages to spin gold from the well-worn thread of a man stuck in time. Whilst this time-loop dramedy might not have been the first film to drink from this particular trope\'s well, it is inarguably head and shoulders above the rest. Murray\'s customarily snarky delivery gets the easy laughs flowing early doors, but it\'s the way the movie finds deeper things to say about existence and morals as it goes on, all whilst never feeling overly preachy or worthy, that keeps us coming back to it again, and again, and again.
